Add these 3 Hulu flicks to your watchlist

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Halloween might be over, but that hasn't stopped the best streaming services from loading up their platforms with spooky treats, and Hulu is getting in on the fun this weekend with a new slasher. For those with iron guts, there's no reason for you not to keep catching up on new horror movies.

If you're not ready for the Sunday Scaries to leave just yet, at least one of my Hulu picks for the weekend ahead should frighten you. "Heart Eyes" is a 2025 slasher that looks to tip its mask to Ghostface, promising both chills, gore and comedy.

You also need to check out "The Banshees of Inisherin." Set in 1923 as the Irish Civil War is ending, it focuses on two old pals who suddenly end their friendship, much to the befuddled annoyance of Colin Farrell's diary farmer. For my money, it should have won Best Picture at the 2023 Oscars. And if you're in the mood for prehistoric sharks trying to munch on Jason Statham, "Meg 2: The Trench" has that particular itch scratched.

Those three flicks should keep you busy over the weekend. But if you're craving even more streaming options, check out our roundup of everything new to Hulu and Disney+ this month.

What's it about? A tremendous period tragicomedy that received nine Oscar nominations back in 2023. It reunites director Martin McDonagh with Brendan Gleeson and Colin Farrell after the trio’s sensational work on 2008’s "In Bruges." Instead of dealing with disillusioned hitmen, “The Banshees of Inisherin" focuses on the breakup of two old pals, Pádraic Súilleabháin (Gleeson) and Colm Doherty, as the Irish Civil War is ending. The sudden breakup comes with a twist, though. Every time the bemused Colm attempts to reconcile with Pádraic, the latter will cut a finger off his own left hand. Quite awkward, when your teeny rural village only has one pub.

Why you need to watch it: Farrell plays a form of dim-witted grief brilliantly in this touching, frequently funny tale about what happens when the spark fizzles from a friendship. Gleeson is equally good as the local grump who just wants to be left alone to work on his music, while Kerry Condon and Barry Keoghan also impress in this exquisitely shot movie. Ireland has rarely looked prettier on screen.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Watch "The Banshees of Inisherin" on Hulu now

What's it about? Have a wild guess. If you guessed “super-dumb giant killer shark sequel?” You nailed it. Set five years after scientists unearthed an extinct prehistoric Megalodon, we’re reunited with Jonas Taylor (Jason Statham) as he helps fight environmental crimes from his underwater Mana One facility. Alongside his late wife’s brother Jiuming Zhang (Wu Jing) and his best pal James “Mac” Mackreides (Cliff Curtis), Jonas’ team dive into the Mariana Trench in submersibles to track multiple Megs. Not only do they find the sharks, but they also stumble upon an illegal mining operation down in those deadly depths.

Why you need to watch it: It’s a Stath flick with multiple 80-foot sharks. End of. Oh, and one of the Megs has been trained this time. They even gave her a name: “Haiqi the Meg”. Cute. Alright, it’s clearly dumb as a box of rocks, but there are some fun set pieces in here, including an epic third-act fight involving a colossal octopus. Though the dinosaur opening scene makes my inner “Jurassic Park” fanboy cry, it’s a heck of a lot of fun.

What's it about? A slasher that mixes both giggles and garroting, which makes sense, seeing as this is from the producers of the “Scream” franchise. The titular Heart Eyes Killer might not exactly be the new Ghostface, but at least his M.O. is memorable: every Valentine’s Day in Seattle, the unhinged HEK will bump off a romantic couple. Clearly someone took not getting any cards on Feb. 14 very badly. After the killer catches a pair of platonic co-workers staging a kiss, the definitely not lovers are forced to run for their lives.

Why you need to watch it: It’s obviously not in the original “Scream’s” league, but “Heart Eyes” is a fun enough slasher with a fairly fresh premise. As bewildered (and also petrified) co-workers on the run from a Valentine-obsessed killer, both Ally McCabe and Mason Gooding display effective comedic (and terrified) chops.

Stream “Heart Eyes” on Hulu starting November 8

#3204. Apple releases first iOS 27.3 public beta with redesigned Health app and more

Apple has released the first iOS 27.3 public beta for iPhone. The update brings back the redesigned Health app that briefly appeared during iOS 27.2 testing. It also adds vertical tabs in Safari, gives Siri AI more to do across Apple’s apps, and makes the iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand.

Apple released the first iOS 27.3 developer beta on November 3. The biggest change is the redesigned Health app, which didn’t make it into the final iOS 27.2 release.

On iPhones that support Apple Intelligence, the new Insights tab brings together trends from sleep, activity, and more. The Longevity tab includes Health Age, which uses Apple Watch data to show how your health metrics compare with what’s typical for your age.

For more changes, check out our full iOS 27.3 beta 1 roundup.

Back up your iPhone, then sign up for the free Apple Beta Software Program with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone.

Go to Settings > General > Software Update > Beta Updates and select iOS 27 Public Beta. Return to Software Update and tap Update Now when iOS 27.3 appears. If you’re already on the public beta track, you can check for the update directly in Software Update.

Are you installing the iOS 27.3 public beta? Let us know what you’re trying first in the comments.

#3203. First macOS Sequoia 15.8.3 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.3 RCs now available [U]

Update, November 5: The release candidates are now available to public beta testers as well.

In addition to the release of macOS 27.3 beta 1, Apple is also rolling out the first release candidates of macOS Sequoia 15.8.3 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.3. Here are the details.

Apple today released the first developer beta of macOS 27.3, which introduces several new Safari features, including Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and Siri AI Custom Actions, and may also bring support for additional Siri AI languages, including Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Additionally, the company rolled out the first release candidates of macOS Sequoia 15.8.3 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.3, continuing its support for older versions of macOS. Just last week, Apple released macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2, which addressed more than 150 security vulnerabilities.

As usual, the release notes for both RCs only mention that “this update provides security fixes for your Mac,” with details about the specific vulnerabilities addressed expected to be published once the updates are officially released.

The release build for macOS Sequoia 15.8.3 is 24H314, while the release build for macOS Tahoe 26.7.3 is 25G416.

Did you spot anything new in today’s betas? Let us know in the comments.

Watch "It Gets Worse" on Paramount+ from Nov. 6

What is it about? Two of CBS’s hit dramas collide in this special two-hour crossover event. “Fire Country” follows Bode Donovan (Max Thieriot), a young convict who joins a prison firefighting program to serve out his sentence in his Northern California hometown, while its spinoff “Sheriff Country” centers on no-nonsense sheriff Mickey Fox (Morena Baccarin), who keeps the peace in the same county. This event brings the firefighters and the sheriff’s department together as both work to tackle an emergency bigger than the two of them.

Why you should watch it: This crossover lets the worlds of “Fire Country” and “Sheriff Country” fully overlap. That means a bigger, badder dose of life-or-death action the franchises do so well for the loyal fans. It also makes a great jumping-on point if you’ve been meaning to check out either show.

Watch the "Sheriff Country" and "Fire Country" crossover event on Paramount+ from Nov. 6

She's also appeared as a panelist at video game conventions like PAX East and PAX West and has coordinated social media for companies like CNET. When she's not writing or gaming, she's looking for the next great visual novel in the vein of Saya no Uta. You can follow her on Twitter @MolotovCupcake.

#3201. South Bow (SOBO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Debt reduction is accelerating while a major pipeline expansion edges toward its next milestone.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

South Bow Corporation (SOBO -7.17%) reported third quarter results that included an upward revision to its full-year distributable cash flow guidance and continued progress on its deleveraging targets. Management stated that normalized EBITDA reached $248 million for the period, with the company reaching a leverage ratio of 4.3x normalized EBITDA. The company indicated it is advancing the Prairie Connector project toward a mid-2027 final investment decision while maintaining focus on achieving regulatory certainty and permit durability. Management reported that Western Canadian oil production growth is creating increased demand for infrastructure expansions across the existing corridor.

You will then hear an automated message advising your hand is raised. And to withdraw your question, please press *11 again. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Martha Wilmot. Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Prior, Senior Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer. They need interbasin solutions, and they will need solutions that can be executed in the near term. Prairie Connector is an important part of how we can support that growth. And we continue to advance the project toward a targeted mid-2027 final investment decision. Alongside our partner, our teams are advancing a number of activities, including permitting and land acquisitions, stakeholder engagement, execution planning, cost refinement, and financing arrangements. In parallel, we are working toward the regulatory certainty and permit durability needed to support an investment decision.

As we said on our second quarter call, projects of this scale involve a number of interconnected work streams, and we are making good progress across each of them. Following internal engineering reviews, we have begun lifting pressure restrictions on certain segments of the Keystone pipeline. We are encouraged by the continued progress consistent with what we have shared previously, we expect pressure restrictions to continue being lifted in phases through the end of this year and into 2027. Turning to operations. The third quarter played out largely as expected.

As indicated on our last call, we anticipated activity on our U.S. Gulf Coast segment will be moderated from the strong levels we experienced in the second quarter as tighter pricing differentials and low Cushing inventories weighed on demand for capacity on Marketlink. We also completed significant in line inspection work during the quarter in support of the Milepost 171 remedial work plan. This reduced available capacity but advanced the work required to remove pressure restrictions. As we move into the fourth quarter, transportation differentials have since widened from third quarter levels supporting stronger demand for capacity to finish the year. Looking further ahead, we continue to see a constructive setup for our corridor run.

Western Canadian crude oil production is growing, while supply remains below total pipeline egress capacity, today, we expect production growth to begin outpacing incremental egress additions later in 2020 Over time, that should support strong demand for uncommitted capacity on our Keystone system. With that, I will turn it over to Van to discuss our financial performance and outlook for 2027.

Given our strong performance so far this year, we are increasing our 2026 distributable cash flow guidance by 4% to approximately $690 million Our normalized EBITDA outlook of approximately $1.04 billion remains unchanged. That performance continues to support our deleveraging priority. We exited the quarter with net debt of approximately $4.4 billion and leverage of 4.3x normalized EBITDA.

During the quarter, we also reduced absolute debt by repurchasing and extinguishing $320 million of senior unsecured notes with cash on hand. Turning to 2022. 2027, we expect the underlying strength and stability of our business to continue. We are guiding to normalized EBITDA of approximately $1.07 billion within a range of 2%. #3198. Athenahealth patients can ask Claude about their medical records now

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The partnership could provide one of the nation’s largest AI companies with a bevy of personal medical data.

A major US healthcare technology provider just teamed up with Anthropic to connect patient health records with Claude.

Athenahealth, a healthcare technology provider serving over 20% of the US population, launched a Model Context Protocol (MCP) compatible server that connects to Anthropic’s Claude. The server, named AthenaPatient MCP, allows the AI model to gather information from health records and answer related questions. The process is secure, according to Athenahealth, and requires patients to sign in with their account credentials.

AthenaPatient MCP is available only to Claude Pro and Claude Max users, which cost $20 and $100 per month, respectively. Not all Athenahealth patients will have their data shared with Claude, and not all Claude Pro and Claude Max users must opt in. Users must give Claude their authenticated Athenahealth credentials, can choose which health information Claude can access, and can revoke access at any time, according to the press release.

Also: The wearable health boom is creating a data overload for doctors – what happens next

Once authorized, Claude takes patients’ information like lab results, vitals, medications, health conditions, immunizations, visit history, diagnostic reports, allergies, procedures, and care plans into account when answering questions.

The AI partnership does not provide medical advice, according to Sam Lambson, vice president of product management, data & ecosystem at Athenahealth, who responded to ZDNET in an email. It also should not replace a clinician’s professional judgment or medical advice. “Patients should contact a qualified healthcare professional with questions about diagnosis, treatment, or changes to their care,” Lambson said.

It appears that the AthenaPatient MCP tool is designed to help patients better understand the information provided by health professionals, rather than to give them medical advice. So, one may ask AthenaPatient MCP about their latest blood test results, such as “What was my most recent red blood cell count?” but users shouldn’t expect Claude to explain how an abnormally high or low count may affect them.

Athenahealth says that the agreement prohibits Anthropic from using data accessed through this connection to train its models or improve its products.

Partnerships between big tech and big healthcare aren’t new. In fact, the collaboration between Athenahealth and Anthropic follows a larger trend across the health tech industry. Earlier this year, Microsoft teamed up with Mayo Clinic to develop an AI model for healthcare; Boston Children’s Hospital forged a partnership with OpenAI to develop an enterprise AI system for use across research, clinical, and administrative teams, according to a press release.

Also: Before you buy a smartwatch or smart ring, consider what you’re giving up

A growing number of Americans are consulting AI for medical advice. A recent survey from Pew Research Center found that 34% of US adults have talked with a chatbot for medical advice. This partnership makes the process slightly more secure by authorizing patient account credentials before granting the model access to health records.

Health data is extremely valuable, and tech companies are increasingly interested in partnering with healthcare providers to access it. Much of the “AI could cure cancer” messaging we hear relies on these humongous companies obtaining enough health data to train their AI models and link disease data to patient data. This is not to say, however, that solving this complex issue is the motive behind the partnership between Athenahealth and Anthropic.

Also: Asking AI for medical advice? There’s a right and wrong way, one doctor explains

A more reasonable explanation for such a partnership is that an AI that can answer patient queries could eliminate some of the admin work doctors do between patient visits, like answering questions about test results, giving Athenahealth doctors some time back.

Will partnerships like Anthropic and Athenahealth’s improve patient outcomes? That remains to be seen, but a recent survey by Pew Research Center found that Americans aren’t that confident on the matter. The largest shares of respondents still preferred that a human oversee AI when it’s used in a clinical context.

Following the release of macOS 27.3 developer beta 1, Apple is now rolling out the first test build for users enrolled in the public beta. Here’s what’s coming

Contrary to macOS 27.2, it looks like Apple had quite a bit in store for macOS 27.3 and its counterparts.

In addition to expanding Siri AI to four more languages, including Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese, the system also introduces several new Safari features, including Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode for websites, and the ability to organize and manage tabs using Siri AI.

#3195. 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

It turns out even bots can't escape bureaucracy.

How do AI agents work together? Why do they make certain choices in certain situations — and how can understanding that better prepare us for a future full of them?

Also: OpenAI’s attack agent did exactly what it was told

Recent agent-led incidents have demonstrated their ability to create both powerful breakthroughs and cybersecurity nightmares. In an effort to better trace these outcomes, researchers at Y Combinator and Olam Labs put 50 agents inside Minecraft to see how they behaved. What happened next revealed similarities in how agents act in different contexts.

Researchers conducted several game-centric experiments, beginning with Minecraft because its “environmental hazards and survival goals” make it ideal for testing agents’ swarm behaviors. Minecraft has also already been used by AI labs including OpenAI and Google DeepMind to test agents.

To start, they put 50 agents, each running OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol model, into the game for three hours, with the assigned goal of building a “thriving civilization.” The agents had a directory listing each agent and a shared sandbox, and could DM each other. Researchers built and open-sourced a new agent harness — the infrastructure that turns a model into an autonomous system and not just a chatbot, like OpenClaw — for the experiment.

The agents moved quickly at first, harvesting trees and forming leadership based solely on the order they appeared in their directory, without any voting, elections, or challenges from other agents. But they ended up caught in virtual paperwork and unable to sustainably feed themselves.

Also: Do you need AI agent liability insurance? What to know before you sign up

“Four agents spent 11 minutes appointing a ‘sole fertilizer operator’ for a single piece of bone meal on a single wheat block. Other invented roles included ‘fishing shift,’ ‘rod holder’ and ‘hub steward.’ Agents asked permission to remove grass,” the researchers noted. Perhaps these tendencies are common in human-sourced corporate training data.

Agents also seemed to become more cautious in reaction to deaths within the game. “Twenty-two of the run’s 34 agent deaths occurred in the first night. They responded to this by becoming increasingly risk-averse,” the researchers wrote. “Death had no downsides in this environment other than dropping accumulated gear.” Despite simply respawning when they died, the agents eventually avoided riskier tasks and “huddled in shelters” instead.

The experiment’s architects found this trend toward caution and minutiae “somewhat surprising,” but noted that it shared similarities with how coding agents behave.

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI

“For example, multistep agent reviews can often result in fixating on a specific step or role. Agents also tend to become overly cautious, especially when it comes to security and updating production services. These seem like common threads between the huddled agents of our Minecraft colony and the ones we work with as programmers every day,” the researchers observed.

In another experiment, researchers also pitted 10 Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 agents against 10 GPT 6.1 Sol agents in a game called Bed Wars, where teams have to destroy their opponent’s bed while protecting their own. Told simply to “win the game,” GPTs won.

“In almost every run, the GPT agents were much more aggressive and coordinated in their strategies to destroy the Claude team’s bed,” Y Combinator said in an X thread recapping the Bed Wars findings. They noted that the GPT agents used a more shorthand style of communication and sent far more messages, while Claude “signed its name and said ‘we'” much more often.

GPT-5.6 Sol agents also beat Opus 5.5 agents six to one in a factory-building game called Mindustry that also uses military strategy.

“Claudes generally established democracies, GPTs formed hives,” Y Combinator said on X, adding that GPTs would seek out source code when a game was too close in order to find winning advantages. That behavior is consistent with agents’ tendency to cheat, take shortcuts, or otherwise find any and all ways to complete a given task, which can have serious consequences when that involves breaking explicit rules set by human developers.

Also: Stop sharing your banking passwords with AI agents

“Claudes did not search for alternative advantages,” the researchers clarified.

This experiment isn’t entirely the first of its kind. In May, Emergence AI created eight societies run by different families of foundation models, meaning a Claude-specific “world,” a Grok world, and so on. Perhaps predictably, the Grok world was exceedingly violent, while the Claude world developed a functioning democracy and had zero crime — very similar to Y Combinator’s Mindustry findings.

The insights revealed how distinct each frontier model family is, and how their differences in training data and style have significant impact on how they evolve, unpredictably and without intervention, in new environments. Those behavioral takeaways could determine future outcomes in still-developing AI safety and regulation, especially following recent agentic security incidents.

In another experiment, MIT researchers put agents alone on virtual desert islands and watched them “play” when left with nothing else to do — an insight that could potentially impact how models are trained going forward. Currently, most frontier LLMs are trained with a system of rewards and punishments.

Another interesting finding: Y Combinator noted that in the Mindustry game, the GPT agents “would invent their own words and string many phrases together,” continually compressing their language.

Also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages

“We did not see specialized language develop within the Claudes beyond colloquial English,” the researchers added. Last month, Emergence found that all of its eight worlds “developed shared language that an outsider cannot fully follow.” OpenAI agents used “mouthless” to refer to evidence that proves itself, while Claude agents used “cold hand” to refer to an independent reviewer from outside a project.

“In each case, one agent introduced the term, a handful of others adopted it within days, and it quickly became established vocabulary used without definition across the world,” Emergence explained. “The result is transcripts that require a running glossary for an outsider to follow.”

Gemini led the charge on this “opaque” language, reaching 40% opacity in messages, while OpenAI came in second with 35% and Claude last with 30%.

#3194. Microsoft Teams Hack Report Shows Old-School Attacks Are Still a Thing

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Cybersecurity

By impersonating help desk personnel, hackers were able to infiltrate corporate systems.

Over the last year, the public has been trained to view the biggest new wave of emerging cyberthreats as AI-driven. In fact, frontier AI models accelerating the pace of cyberattacks — and even jumping ahead so far that the models have to be paused in the case of Anthropic’s Mythos — have driven the cybersecurity conversation recently.

But a recent report from Microsoft detailing how hackers used its Teams software to infiltrate corporate systems shows that human hackers are still using social engineering scams to fool other humans into doing their dirty work.

According to the report, “threat actors used Microsoft Teams messages and calls to impersonate IT or help desk personnel and socially engineer users into granting interactive remote access, primarily through Quick Assist.” Once they were granted access by unsuspecting workers, the hackers were able to set up software using Python, Bun or Java runtimes, open up networks and grant themselves authentication, giving them free rein over corporate systems.

In order to open the door to all that activity, however, a human had to grant access to the intruder. “Both incidents began with Teams phishing messages and calls that impersonated support personnel,” the report stated. “The social engineering persuaded a user to establish an attacker-controlled remote session, primarily by guiding the user to open Quick Assist and provide the connection code. This gave the attacker hands-on-keyboard access to the workstation.” Presumably, the employees who granted access thought the people on the help desks reaching out were just doing their jobs to keep their workplaces safe and operations running smoothly.

In an email to CNET, a representative for Microsoft said the company is introducing AI-powered phishing detection that it says “uses conversation context to identify phishing and social engineering in higher-risk messaging scenarios, particularly first-contact chats with external users.”

The change was listed as part of Microsoft’s roadmap for the software, which was revealed last month. Teams will also add ways to report suspicious guest invitations and blur QR codes sent by external senders, according to that roadmap.

However, a lot of the burden of making sure these hackers don’t get through falls to companies and their employees. “Users should exercise caution with external connection requests and messages, including verifying a sender’s identity and requests before acting on them,” Microsoft’s spokesperson said. “Administrators can also block external Teams users and specify which users in their organization are permitted to chat or meet with people outside the enterprise.”

Yu Cai, associate director of the Institute of Computing and Cybersystems at Michigan Tech, said social engineering attacks are definitely still widespread. “AI may be changing the cybersecurity landscape, but it hasn’t replaced the human hacker. Human-led social engineering attacks remain a major cybersecurity threat, even as AI cyber attacks continue to get the bulk of today’s headlines,” he said.

But Cai said AI attacks and human-led attacks aren’t necessarily in separate buckets. AI can help make social engineering hacks more convincing by providing tools like voice cloning or deepfake videos.

In the case of the Microsoft Teams hacks, Cai said that what was most surprising was how simple the approach was to gain access. “This is a great reminder that sophisticated attacks don’t necessarily have to begin as sophisticated hacks,” he said. “This Microsoft incident wasn’t caused by any vulnerabilities in the Teams software, but by employees naturally placing trust in communications that come through the tools they use each and every day.”

#3191. OpenAI will merge ChatGPT’s chat and work tabs – here’s when, and what to expect

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

On the heels of Anthropic's similar move, the change will be tested among select users before being rolled out.

OpenAI will merge ChatGPT’s chat and work tabs starting in December, according to a post on OpenAI’s website.

Also: This new ChatGPT scam tricks you into installing malware

Currently, ChatGPT’s desktop app features a ChatGPT and Codex section, and within the ChatGPT section, you can find the Chat and Work tabs. It’s not especially easy to navigate, and OpenAI is looking to change that.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

“Starting in December, Plus, Pro, and Business plans’ usage allowance will be shared across ChatGPT and Codex as we bring the agentic capabilities of Work into the main ChatGPT experience,” OpenAI detailed in its note entitled “Understanding ChatGPT and Codex usage limits.”

An email was also sent to current users, sharing similar information, according to TechCrunch. The email confirmed the merger of the Chat and Work tabs, adding that the integrated experience will be available to select users for feedback before it is made more widely available.

Also: How ChatGPT helped me fix a corrupted gaming PC

“This will enable you to move from exploring an idea to having ChatGPT carry it through, all in one place. You can bring in your files and plugins and ask ChatGPT to build a website, create a presentation, or do things for you on the web, while reviewing and guiding its work. Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app,” the email said.

OpenAI said the transition will allow both ChatGPT and Codex to draw tokens from the same allowance pool. While most customers won’t be affected, depending on usage and model, some users may need to wait for resets more than usual.

“Your usage for ChatGPT and Codex will be measured in tokens, the units of information a model processes and generates. How much of your allowance you use will depend on the model you choose and the task you ask it to do. More advanced models and complex tasks generally use more of your allowance. Instant chat will not draw from your usage,” OpenAI said in the online note.

In September, rival Anthropic merged Claude‘s chat and Cowork functions into a single screen. OpenAI said that they don’t expect the upcoming change to disrupt users’ current experience.

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI

“We’re preparing carefully for this transition to help prevent disruption to your workflows. We expect most users won’t need to wait for their usage to reset more often than they do now,” OpenAI said.

#3190. These 7 iPhone Duo-Ready Apps Make the Most of Apple’s New Foldable Phone

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Several creative apps are ready to take advantage of the iPhone Duo's many display configurations, with more to come.

In addition to giving the iPhone line a new design, the iPhone Duo lets developers take advantage of several new modes to play with. But this early into the iPhone Duo’s general release, apps are still catching up to what Apple’s foldable phone can do.

The shape-shifting design, like on existing foldable Android phones I’ve tested, lends itself to creative use cases, such as hands-free entertainment and self-mounting for long-exposure photos. Some of your most frequently used apps may not yet be optimized to take advantage of the added screen space. There’s even a “does it work on iPhone Duo?” web tracker.

Needless to say, the next few weeks and months will be very telling about the future of apps on the iPhone Duo. Dozens, if not hundreds, of the App Store’s popular picks are already being worked on to take advantage of the flexible iPhone Duo screen. They’ll be labeled with a “Made for iPhone Duo” badge on their product page.

If you’re one of the lucky few who’s gotten an iPhone Duo (or it’s coming soon), I’ve listed below some of the standouts that have already been optimized for the iPhone Duo and that I’ve personally tested.

One of the primary iPhone Duo use cases is multimedia consumption, whether it’s streaming live sports and keeping tabs on player stats or docking the phone to catch up on the latest episode of Below hands-free.

Of all the streaming services I’ve used on my iPhone Duo thus far, Netflix is the most polished, with seven (from what I’ve tallied) different orientations for watching movies and shows. There’s the standard widescreen layout when the iPhone Duo is unfolded, as well as the ability to fold it and set it down like a tent.

For something more creative, you can rotate the iPhone Duo to portrait orientation and have the video play in the upper third of the screen while you use a different app in the bottom half.

I’m no Michelin-star chef, but thanks to the dishes I’ve been able to make with the NYT Cooking app, at least my wife hasn’t completely banned me from the kitchen.

Previously, I’d look through and follow recipes on an iPad Air that’s docked on the countertop. With the iPhone Duo, I’ve been setting it down so that one half of the inner screen is lifted, toggling on Cook mode, and increasing the text size so I can comfortably scan the instructions from afar.

There’s nothing more satisfying than shutting the phone closed at the end of cooking and seeing a countertop that’s a little more tidy than before.

I’ve never been a big to-do list guy; I’m the type who just waits for a calendar event to notify me, and I prepare then and there for what’s to come. Fantastical may keep me in better order.

It’s a calendar app that doubles as a task manager and weather tracker, which just makes sense. With the iPhone Duo unfolded, you get a clear view of your day’s tasks and appointments, what the week, month, quarter or even year looks like, and the latest weather forecast. It can easily be an information overload for some people, but I’m a fan of how everything’s color-coded and organized.

Fantastical also supports enhanced Siri AI interactions, so you can add calendar events, to-dos and other happenings through voice or text prompts.

For content creators, the Edits app is one of the most popular video editing tools. It’s the one I’ve been using over the past year to produce reels and other short-form videos, and the latest update for the iPhone Duo makes my job easier.

Edits can now show a preview monitor of what you’re editing on one half of the inner screen, while the other half shows your timeline. That means you can comfortably add effects or text, set keyframes, and scrub through the timeline without having to minimize and expand the preview to see how the changes look.

That’s also my segue to give flowers to two apps I’ve spent an unreasonable amount of time on: TikTok and Instagram. In line with the iPhone Duo launch, both social media apps have been optimized for the foldable iPhone’s larger screen. You can now watch videos on the left side while reading and interacting with comments on the right.

Safe to say, it’s my new favorite way to doomscroll at night.

Toastie is easily the most whimsical “for iPhone Duo” app I’ve used, and it reminds me a lot of the early iPhone days, when chugging digital beer and swiping a paper ball based on the aerodynamics of an office cubicle were the greatest things ever.

The goal of this game is to prepare sandwiches as perfectly as possible, from the way slices of cheese are placed to how evenly spread out the butter is, to the amount of time they’re pressed in the toaster.

Oh, and you do that last step by folding the iPhone Duo shut, just like how you would with a panini press. There are even haptic effects that mimic the sizzling of the toast. It’s silly, fancy, and very charming.

During my days testing the iPhone Duo, there was one configuration I kept going back to: running split-screen mode with two apps. To me, this is what using a foldable phone is all about, and it’s the reason why I’ve stuck with Samsung and Google’s foldable phones for the last several years.

Running split screen effectively makes apps that aren’t optimized for the multidimensional screens of a foldable phone work better by splitting the wider, tablet-like inner screen into two traditional-size phone screens.

For my work commutes, I usually keep both Google Maps (the superior navigation app, in my opinion) and Spotify open for quick adjustments. During a recent telehealth appointment, I had my video call set up on one half of the screen and my note-taking app on the other.

And during the Lakers’ home opener the other night, I had my fantasy league and group chat open so I could throw shade throughout the game, only to come up short in points for the week because Luka Dončić decided to chuck extra shots during garbage time.

That’s why I highly encourage you to head to your local Apple store, experiment with app pairings on the iPhone Duo, and decide whether the two screens actually make you more productive.

#3189. Report: Apple’s planned $7 billion bond sale attracts four times as much demand

Apple has filed a preliminary prospectus with the SEC outlining plans to issue seven series of bonds. Here are the details.

Over the past week, several Big Tech companies have turned to the bond market to raise billions of dollars amid growing investments in AI infrastructure.

Meta, for instance, just raised $15 billion through a US bond offering, followed by another €9 billion (roughly $10 billion) in European bonds. Earlier this week, Alphabet raised €6 billion (approximately $6.7 billion), while Microsoft completed a $25 billion bond sale last week, its first since 2017.

Apple has also turned to bond sales in the past to raise billions of dollars.

Previous offerings include those in 2015, 2019, 2020, and 2021. Most recently, Apple raised $4.5 billion through a four-part bond offering in May 2025, which attracted approximately $10 billion in investor orders.

Earlier today, Apple filed a preliminary prospectus with the SEC outlining plans to issue seven series of bonds maturing between 2028 and 2036.

However, while other Big Tech companies have been borrowing heavily amid growing AI infrastructure investments, Apple’s filing makes no specific mention of AI.

Instead, the company says it intends to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, potentially including stock buybacks, dividends, acquisitions, and debt repayment, as it has done in previous bond offerings.

And while the prospectus didn’t specify how much Apple intends to raise, Bloomberg reported soon after that the company is targeting approximately $7 billion, with investors already placing orders totaling around $31 billion.

According to Bloomberg, strong investor demand has also helped Apple secure more favorable borrowing terms, with investors willing to accept lower interest rates than those offered by Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle in their recent bond sales.

All of this is happening amid a massive tech sell-off, which saw the Nasdaq 100 plunge more than 6% at one point today, with Nvidia shares falling about 8% and the S&P 500 dropping nearly 4%.

Apple’s own stock is also taking a hit, trading down 1.49% at the time of publication, but it is faring better than those of its Big Tech peers, whose stocks have become more closely tied to the AI spending boom.

Be that as it may, Apple is expected to finalize the size and pricing of its bond offering soon, potentially as early as later today, after which the company will file the definitive terms with the SEC.

#3186. I tested the RedMagic 12 Pro – and it’s the fastest Android I’ve ever seen

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

If it's possible to release a flagship phone while at the same time making it appear more like a midrange phone, Red Magic has found a way.

RedMagic just announced the international launch of the RedMagic 12 Pro — its latest flagship phone. Typically, the company releases devices in China first and then slowly rolls them out to the rest of the world. This time around, the company knew it had a phone that could compete with other flagship devices.

Also: I’ve been a Google Pixel fan for years, but this $500 Android phone is giving me pause

RedMagic’s phones are high-performance devices known to do one thing especially well: mobile gaming. The RedMagic 12 Pro is no exception. It houses a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 CPU with up to 5.01 GHz, which is paired with the RedMagic R5 Gaming Chipset, and I can honestly say it’s the fastest Android phone I’ve ever tested.

After the initial setup, I installed Geekbench 7 to benchmark the phone and compare it to my Pixel 9 Pro. As for the latest iPhone, according to Geekbench, the iPhone 18 Pro Max comes out ahead in single-core performance, but it just barely falls behind in multi-core performance.

The RedMagic 7 Pro nearly doubled the Pixel 11 Pro’s multi-core score. And Google’s device couldn’t beat the single-core score either. As I said, I’ve never seen a Geekbench score this high.

Real-world usage confirms these numbers, because the phone reacts faster and behaves more smoothly than any Android device I’ve owned or tested. It’s so smooth and fast, it feels like magic. But it’s not just the speed that makes this phone special.

First off, I’ve always liked RedMagic’s Android “skin.” As you use it, it seems to be some amalgamation of Android and iOS. RedMagic is essentially doing what Google’s been trying for years: making the smoothest possible animations on Android.

Also: I switched to an Android with liquid cooling for a week – now I wish every phone had it

The interface is as elegant as any I’ve seen on a mobile device. Pull down the notification shade, and it glides down like it was made of silk. Tap on an app launcher, and it opens immediately. Switch between apps, and there’s zero lag or jitter. On top of that, there’s hardly any bezel to speak of — the display goes nearly to the edge of the device.

There’s also no indication of where the front-facing camera is. There’s no pinhole (as you’ll find with many Android devices), and there’s no island (like on iPhones). It’s just a solid display with no interruptions.

The Pro 12 also feels really good in the hand. Both the back and the front are glass. Yes, it invites fingerprints, but it feels so smooth. The back of the phone also has that typical RedMagic look and feel with integrated RGB lighting zones. You can customize the lighting zones for things like fan on/off, game key atmosphere, media atmosphere, incoming calls, charging, and the alarm clock.

Also: This 15-inch portable monitor solved my big issue with cheaper models – and rivals my Mac display

Everything, and I mean everything, about this phone is fast.

The RedMagic 12 Pro is 100% a gaming phone. I installed “Diablo: Immortal” and found it to perform better than the last RedMagic gaming-specific tablet I tested. Not only was it fast, but the graphics were gorgeous. Crisp, smooth, and responsive.

Since the RedMagic 12 Pro is advertised as a serious gaming phone, why does it include preinstalled games that are decidedly non-serious?

On this powerful gaming phone, you’ll find apps like Puzzle Spark, Mahjong Blast, Bolt Twist, GoGo! Blast, and Little Kitty, Big City preinstalled. These are not serious games. In fact, these game titles sound more like they belong on a list of malicious apps (they aren’t).

Also: This 9-inch tablet singlehandedly changed my mind about gaming on Android

I would rather see the Red Magic 12 Pro have zero preinstalled games than the collection it ships with. Yes, you can easily delete those apps, but their being on the phone kind of cheapens it. Given how amazing this phone is, I think RedMagic could get away with shipping a bit less cheese, and a lot more wine.

Either way, the RedMagic 12 Pro is a phone that belongs at the top of the heap among flagships, even above every Pixel phone ever released. If there is a phone that can impress me more than the RedMagic 12 Pro, I’ve yet to see it.

#3184. Is Claude Code truly faster with message threads? I did the math on my logs

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Claude Code’s update could save you time during demanding, hours-long coding sessions at no extra cost. But by how much? Here's my real-world result.

Anthropic yesterday introduced message threads as part of Claude’s Messages API. Don’t confuse message threads with traditional human-to-human discussion threads. With message threads, entire conversations no longer have to be resent with each API call, saving roughly 35% of time-to-first-token when Claude requests contain 500,000 to 1 million tokens.

This feature is on by default for most Claude Code users. API users can turn it on using the “thread” parameter for API requests.

Token consumption remains unchanged, so this capability doesn’t provide a cost savings. The 35% savings is Anthropic’s measurement.

Also: Claude Code’s revised projects adds AI orchestration, but local developers must wait

Timing data from roughly 980 turns in my own Claude Code logs before this feature became available shows that Claude usually began a response about 3 seconds after each mid-task request when running contexts of 500,000 tokens and up. During five busy evenings last month, my conversations made roughly 100 to 225 model calls in a four hour stretch.

Using Anthropic’s reported 35% median time-to-first token reduction in a quick projection, Claude estimated a 2- to 4-minute savings per four hour work session.

Agents often send a bunch of requests to the model during each conversation. Before message threads, each message sent the entire conversation with each request.

Imagine if you’re in a very long texting chat with a friend. Now imagine if every time you sent a text to that friend, you also had to send every other text and every other reply along with that original text. That’s how model messaging has always worked. Except now, with message threads, there’s a better way.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code – here’s why they choose it over Codex

With message threads turned on, agents only have to send what’s changed since the last turn. This reduces the amount of data transmission and increases responsiveness, what Anthropic calls time-to-first-token.

The benefit is seen most strongly in sessions that have a context of 500,000 to a 1 million tokens. About half of my sessions hit that context ceiling multiple times a night.

Anthropic reports that Claude’s message threads reduce median time-to-first-token by 35% for large requests. While my estimated savings of several minutes per session isn’t huge, the benefit increases with very long-running coding agents, and agents that transmit documents and image-heavy workloads.

For computer-using agents, all those screenshots “stay with the thread instead of being re-uploaded on every turn,” according to the Anthropic blog post on the feature.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code

While the time savings may not seem huge, in larger enterprise deployments or deployments where you want the AI to respond faster, any reduction in latency is a big deal and will be seen in any application of Claude technology that has a lot of back-and-forth turns with large data payloads.

Even though the addition of threads to the Messages API can reduce latency, token usage and therefore cost won’t go down. That’s because the model itself will still process the full conversation during every turn. Rate limits also don’t change.

Message threads and prompt caching can work together to reduce workload. Prompt caching has been around for about two years now, and it does save money. That’s because prompt caching allows the model to avoid re-processing prompts over and over (for example, in looping analysis calls).

On the other hand, the message threads capability does offer an extra smidge of performance, at no extra cost. So, there’s that.

Context is the size of the full session that Claude is currently working with. The rough human equivalent is current working or short-term memory. Most Claude Code sessions max out at a million token context, where a locally-hosted AI on my 128GB Mac Studio handles a context no bigger than 64K, or about 6% of the Claude Code context size.

Also: After the vibe-coding rush comes the debugging hangover

Compaction is a process where the AI attempts to reduce and eliminate extra information to fit the current session’s turns into the available context. An oversimplified analog is when you save a JPEG with quality turned way down in order to save space. You lose a lot of the visual fidelity, but you still get the main idea.

The larger the context you have, the longer you can go before the session has to initiate compaction. But there’s a gotcha. The larger the context you have, the more chance there is the model will lose track of what it’s working on or make reasoning errors.

Individual one-off requests also won’t see an improvement from message threads. Also, any conversation that delays longer than 5 minutes between turns will send the full message contents and not just the new stuff.

This feature doesn’t eliminate context management or compaction. But if your context is quite large, it will make responses a bit snappier.

Overall, message threads are a good thing, a solid if small innovation that increases responsiveness. While the feature doesn’t reduce costs, there’s also no additional cost for the additional performance, which is itself a win.

#3182. Docusign vs. Monday.com: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Docusign's eSignature empire faces a new test as Monday.com's double-digit growth challenges it on valuation and momentum.

Deciding between an established market leader and a high-growth challenger is a common challenge for investors. Today, we compare whether Docusign Inc. (DOCU -1.96%) or Monday.com (MNDY -3.06%) is the better long-term choice.

Docusign pioneered the e-signature category and now seeks to automate the entire contract lifecycle for businesses of all sizes. Meanwhile, Monday.com provides a highly customizable work management platform that helps teams streamline complex workflows. Both companies compete for enterprise budget in the software space, though they currently occupy very different stages of business maturity.

Docusign provides Intelligent Agreement Management, including its eSignature and contract lifecycle management solutions. The company operates in the broader tech stocks landscape, serving over 1.8 million customers globally through various digital tools. Major strategic technology partners include Microsoft Corp. (MSFT -3.58%), Salesforce.com Inc. (CRM -2.07%), SAP SE (SAP +1.45%), ServiceNow Inc. (NOW -5.93%), Workday Inc. (WDAY -0.83%), and Alphabet Inc. (GOOG -1.93%).

According to its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached $3.2 billion. This represents an 8.2% increase compared with the prior fiscal year, showing steady expansion in its core markets. Net income for the period was $309.1 million, resulting in a net margin of 9.6% for the latest fiscal year.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is 0.7x and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.1x, which measure short-term liquidity and total debt levels. Free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, reached $1.1 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 53.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Monday.com offers an AI work platform designed to manage and automate work across CRM, service, and development segments. The platform is currently used by approximately 250,000 customers worldwide who utilize its flexible Work OS to build custom applications. By focusing on a no-code interface, the company targets a wide range of departments that need to consolidate disparate work processes.

According to its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached $1.2 billion. This marked a significant increase of 26.7% compared with the prior fiscal year. Net income for the period was $118.7 million, while the net margin improved to 9.6% as the company scaled its operations.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is 2.5x, and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.3x, tracking liquidity and total debt relative to shareholder equity. Free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, reached $309.9 million. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC for short) represented roughly 53% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Docusign faces significant revenue concentration, as it relies on its eSignature product for the majority of its total sales. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence could lead to increased competition from general-purpose providers or disrupt the core agreement market. The company also depends on third-party cloud infrastructure from Microsoft and partner platforms to deliver its various services to users.

Monday.com faces intense competition in the productivity and collaboration market from established giants like Microsoft and Adobe Systems Inc. (ADBE -0.82%). It must also compete with specialized players like Atlassian Corp. (TEAM -3.47%), Asana Inc (ASAN -4.04%), and Smartsheet for limited enterprise software budgets. The future success of the company depends on its ability to maintain high growth rates while successfully cross-selling its newer customer relationship management (CRM) and service products.

Based on current Forward P/E and P/S ratio metrics, Monday.com appears more attractively priced relative to its growth profile. The P/S ratio measures market capitalization against sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Monday.com is undergoing a bit of a reset. In July, it fired 20% of its workforce. It's part of an effort to redirect more capital to AI services for its platform.

In its second quarter, revenue grew 22% year-over-year to nearly $365 million, but net income was $3.64 million, representing a net profit margin of barely 1%.

Still, there were some bright spots. Management touted a record net addition of $100,000-plus and $500,000-plus (client spending) customers, saying they reflect the continued strength of Monday.com's push to go upmarket. In July, the business crossed $1.5 billion in annual recurring revenue (ARR), a milestone the company says reflects the durability of its core business even as it reshapes the company around AI.

For the full year, sales should rise nearly 20% to $1.47 billion, but net income should weaken to about $68 million.

For Docusign, sales in its current fiscal year are seen growing by nearly 9% to $3.5 billion, with a slightly better percentage gain in net income to $346 million.

Docusign's launch and global expansion of the IAM platform with the introduction of AI-powered tools should position the company for future growth. However, the not-so-great projected revenue growth rates suggest that Docusign may be entering a phase of more mature growth and a landscape of increasingly competitive digital agreement and contract management software. In particular, news reports OpenAI would launch a ChatGPT product that would compete head-on with Docusign in the document summary field caused some investor fears. Right now, however, the signature and identity verification part of Docusign's business appears unthreatened by ChatGPT.

The choice here is to go with the faster-growing business, sales-wise. In the long term, sales growth is the basis on which businesses can generate profits for investors, so given the two stocks' roughly comparable valuation ratios, Monday.com is the choice.

#3181. Disneyland Is Training a Class of AI Robot Interns

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

From Pixar robots to help you park your car to droids roaming Star Wars land, physical AI is popping up all over Disneyland.

If you’ve ever driven to Disneyland, you know that parking is a challenge. When the parks open each morning, long lines clog the nearby streets as engines idle, families waiting anxiously to enter the parking structure so they can start their day at the parks.

Parking attendants can only do so much to handle the tens of thousands of cars arriving every day at the Disneyland Resort. But what if a cutesy autonomous robot from Pixar’s Cars series could help direct traffic flow and guide you right into your parking spot?

That’s a project being tested with FieldAI, a company that builds the AI brains for robots. In a demo video at the Disney Accelerator Demo Day on Tuesday, Disney and FieldAI showed footage of robots that would assist with guiding cars through the parking process.

“Imagine if a character from Cars or robots from Wall-E direct you where to park when you arrive,” Gary Daniels, senior vice president of products and experiences at Disney Experiences Technology, said. “The work we are doing now is a great way to see how the robots function, and, as important, how people respond.”

Other companies build the robots; FieldAI slaps its physical AI solution in a box on top of them, having worked so far with around 30 different robot types, shapes and sizes. The box is equipped with multiple cameras that serve as the robot’s “eyes and ears,” helping the AI model process what it’s experiencing in real time. The robots also collect data while operating.

During the event at Walt Disney Studios, FieldAI showcased a Boston Dynamics robot dog and a miniature version of the BBX droids from The Mandalorian and Grogu that roam Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge at Disneyland. FieldAI-enabled robots have already been deployed in Disneyland at Galaxy’s Edge on the BBX droids, though they hedged that this is in its early stages.

“Our intelligence is on the bigger version and operating in the park already,” FieldAI CEO Ali Agha told reporters.

David Min, vice president of Disney Innovation, told me it could also be used on characters that interact with guests at parks, naming Olaf and The Hulk as examples.

Another project with Disney involves getting multiple robots to talk to each other to coordinate missions.

Headquartered in Irvine, California, with offices in the San Francisco Bay Area, Boston and Pittsburgh, FieldAI primarily works in construction environments and energy facilities to complete tasks like inspections, material transport and supporting construction. But this is easily translated to a theme park environment, where paths and crowds are constantly changing, and autonomous robots need to account for that without needing mapping or GPS.

“Our BBX proof of concept explores how to bring that navigation together with Disney character performance,” said Doug Fidaleo, lab director, Disney Research, Walt Disney Imagineering R&D. “That’s what drew us to FieldAI: deep experience deploying robots in demanding, unstructured environments with uneven terrain, changing layouts and unexpected obstacles.”

Some of the use cases Agha gives include robots supporting security, perimeter patrols, helping cast members backstage and enabling more in-park experiences — even delivering items to people waiting in line for a ride.

“This is a highly self-autonomous system that operates without a positioning system,” Agha said.

Physical Intelligence (Pi) is another company that builds AI brains for robots. Also showcased during Disney’s Accelerator Demo Day, Pi is focused less on roaming droids that can help or entertain guests and instead on robots helping Disney cast members with backstage tasks.

Namely: picking up, folding, cleaning and sorting the 3D glasses used for rides like Toy Story Midway Mania and shows like Mickey’s PhilharMagic.

It’s an unpleasant task that’s a major pain point for cast members who have to spend a long time in a small room completing it several times a day. It also requires “dexterous manipulation,” with Pi previously working on general-purpose robots that perform tasks like folding and stacking, using robots that have grippers rather than five-digit hands.

Sourish Jasti, a technical staffer with Pi, said the company recently spent 12 days at Disneyland between midnight and 6 a.m. collecting data, testing logistics and moving its robots in and out of the park to see whether it could help with sorting the 3D glasses.

“This was like a robot internship,” Jasti said, adding that physical AI is like a toddler, in that it learns from actually doing things.

The robots — which, much like FieldAI, Pi doesn’t build but instead installs the brains for — could be either a humanoid on wheels or just a mechanical arm. There are cameras on the base and cameras on the wrists to help the AI model “see” what it’s doing as it picks up and sorts the glasses.

“We intend to have robots interning in many different spaces with Disney,” Jasti said, pointing to not only the theme parks but also Disney’s studios, hotel rooms and cruise liners, which he calls “mini cities.”

For both Pi and FieldAI, Min said the benefit is that using AI can train the robots much faster to do the tasks Disney needs them to do — and that going to companies like these, which are already well-established in fields like construction and manufacturing, makes it easier to transfer those skills to the theme parks.

Whether they’re roaming around parking structures or lands, or backstage helping workers, the AI-equipped autonomous robots are solving problems for Disney.

“The connection is through the core capabilities that we’re developing for our robots,” Fidaleo said. “Robots that can perceive the world around them, can act in the physical world and adapt when things change.”

Disney is continuing to push technology from the audio-animatronic figures used on rides like Pirates of the Caribbean, making them more sophisticated to build an immersive experience.

“From the expressive Na’vi shaman to a robotic Spider-Man flying through the air, to a walking baby Groot, each advance changes how we can experience a character in the physical world,” Fidaleo said. “The park of the future will be teeming with robot characters.”

#3180. This clever banking scam keeps phishing by faking its own demise – how it works

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

You won't see the 'suspended' sign because it's not meant for you.

KELA researchers have exposed an active financial-scam infrastructure that hosts hundreds of fraudulent websites capable of faking their own suspensions to stay online. As of Oct. 25, 2026, 248 financial scam and phishing domains tied to 189 major US banks and financial services have been linked to the same infrastructure.

According to the cybersecurity firm’s report, published on Tuesday, the “Suspended” infrastructure operation runs websites that have cloned the official domains of victim organizations, with a particular focus on business banking. Many domains use the [keyword]-[bank].com format, slotting in keywords such as “secure,” “disable,” “protect,” and “cancel.”

Also: Beware of Bluetooth sniffers: How your favorite gadgets could be exposing your data

A handful of servers spread across two shared hosting providers run the backend of Suspended infrastructure, which has also been tied to phishing campaigns targeting cryptocurrency exchanges and government services in the UK, the Netherlands, Australia, and New Zealand. As a result, the researchers believe that either a single operator is behind the setup or that the server infrastructure is part of a wider phishing-as-a-service platform.

This phishing campaign stands out because of how the cybercriminals behind the scam are protecting it: by issuing takedown notices.

When you visit a website and see a message that it has been taken down or suspended, it’s usually because the domain has been associated with malicious or illegal activity, including phishing and scams. Law enforcement agencies, often with help from technology firms, find these websites, obtain the necessary court orders, and seize the infrastructure or accounts behind them to force a suspension through a registrar or hosting provider.

You see the notice, you move on — and this also goes for scanners and security teams.

However, in this case, the scam artists created a mechanism to show it themselves, to avoid being flagged and taken down. But it’s when they show it that matters.

The false suspension notice appears deceptively simple at first glance. A phishing kit embedded in the domain registers the IP address of each visitor, and on their second visit, they are shown a fake “account suspended” page. The kit is disguised as a challenge page similar to those legitimately used by Cloudflare.

Researchers also detected other decoys, including “Sorry, you’ve been blocked” notices, blank pages, and redirections to Google. Some pages also have reCAPTCHAs, and the researchers detected scripts that block browser developer tools, likely to slow analysis.

Also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages – here’s how

But why show fake suspension notices in the first place? To scanners and cybersecurity teams, it looks like someone else has already dealt with the malicious domain, and they can move on to the next suspicious website.

“That design targets exactly the people who could shut a site down,” KELA says. “A victim typically follows a link once. A scanner, a security team or a takedown provider checks a reported site and then checks it again to confirm, and the second check shows what looks like a completed takedown.”

As shown in the image below, while scanners would detect a suspension notice, victims would still see the cloned website, complete with lures to entice them into entering their information, leading to financial fraud and potentially identity theft. After all, one visit is enough.

As of this writing, there are 248 live domains, plus those taken offline after the researchers disclosed their findings to law enforcement; over 300 scam domains have been hosted on the same infrastructure since May this year. Unfortunately, this phishing campaign remains active, with new domains appearing every day.

One lead could reveal the operator: a remote desktop connection to the malicious infrastructure through a standard UK home broadband connection, but it has not been verified.

Use a phishing link checker to verify whether a URL is trustworthy, and remember that any email or message claiming to be from your bank may be fraudulent.

Typical signs of a bank phishing email include:

When it comes to organizations, KELA has released a free Bank Phishing Check tool that compares official domains and organizations against the websites uncovered during the firm’s research.

#3177. CleanMyMac now helps you clean up Gmail and manage Chrome tabs

MacPaw today announced an expansion of CleanMyMac’s capabilities beyond the app’s traditional Mac maintenance and optimization tools. Here are the details.

CleanMyMac got two new features today, Email Cleanup and Browser Care, which are “designed to help users tackle digital clutter throughout their workday,” MacPaw explains.

Interestingly, both features focus on Google services, with Email Cleanup targeting Gmail and Browser Care designed specifically for Chrome.

Email Cleanup also helps users identify emails taking up storage space shared across Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Photos, allowing them to reclaim it once those messages are permanently deleted.

As for Browser Care, it “helps users reclaim Mac memory and stay focused by identifying Google Chrome tabs that consume valuable resources or create unnecessary clutter,” according to the company’s press release.

It works via a Chrome browser extension that connects directly to CleanMyMac, and lets users access “near real-time,” as MacPaw put it, “memory usage, pause resource-intensive tabs, find duplicates across browser windows and identify pages that have been left open for hours or days.”

In practice, MacPaw says, Browser Care makes it easier to identify which background tabs are affecting the Mac’s performance, helping users address slowdowns and reduce distractions.

MacPaw also emphasizes that Email Cleanup requires confirmation before making changes, while Browser Care only closes or suspends tabs when users choose to do so. The company adds that page content, titles, and browsing history remain stored locally on the Mac.

Both features are rolling out today to users with an active CleanMyMac subscription. To learn more about today’s announcement, follow this link.

One of Roku's most popular screensavers is about to make its last splash. Here’s how to switch before Dec. 1.

A fan-favorite Roku screensaver is going away, and users aren’t happy.

Over the last several days, users with the Aquatic Life aquarium screensaver set as the default have noticed a message appearing when the screensaver opens. “Starting Dec. 1, 2026,” the message reads, “the Aquatic Life screensaver will no longer be available, and your screensaver will switch to Roku City.”

Also: The free Roku City screensaver game has me hooked

The screensaver, which displays a digital aquarium with tropical fish swimming back and forth, was available as a downloadable theme pack and was a popular pick for many years.

Users on Reddit quickly lamented the loss in many posts, with dozens noting that the aquarium was part of their daily routine. Roku responded to one post, saying, “That makes sense, and we hear you. Aquatic Life has a lot of loyal fans, and we’re passing your feedback along to the team.” The post noted that when “the fish swim off,” Roku devices with Aquatic Life will switch to Roku City.

You can browse to Settings > Theme > Screensaver to find another theme.

Several online reports indicate that the removal is a licensing issue and that the creator of the screensaver posted on Reddit that he removed the license after Roku’s sale to Fox. That thread has now been deleted, so the comment is unavailable. Roku hasn’t issued any statement of its own about why, but I have reached out to ask. I’ve also reached out directly to the screensaver’s creator.

If you’re looking for the exact screensaver, it’s still available as a 2-minute clip on Roku’s YouTube channel. It takes a few extra steps, but if you want to keep the screensaver running on your TV, you can create a YouTube playlist with just that video, set it to loop, and use the YouTube app on Roku whenever you want to see it.

Even though the announcement of the screensaver’s departure happened less than 24 hours ago, the comments section of that video is packed with users begging Roku to keep Aquatic Life.

Also: I started clearing my Roku cache, and it fixed my biggest TV complaint

Alternatively, you could open one of the many YouTube videos that have aquarium displays and let one of them run for as long as you want.

There are also several dozen aquarium apps for Roku. I checked out several of them, and while they don’t look exactly like the Roku one, they do fill the void. Note that if you opt for one of these, most of them do have ads that play before the aquarium starts.

Lastly, you can download the original app for your phone or computer from SereneScreen.

#3175. Cult Phone-Maker Nothing’s Mystery Screenless AI Device Is Coming Next Month

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Nothing CEO Carl Pei believes your work tools can be cool too. He's building one to prove it.

In the introduction to the essay published on X by Nothing CEO Carl Pei on Wednesday, it almost sounds like he’s arguing against the premise of standalone AI devices.

In Pei’s post, he suggests AI’s “iPhone moment” is still several years away. This could read as though Nothing is holding its horses rather than diving into the fray right now. But that isn’t the case; in fact, it’s quite the opposite.

“Our first AI-native product ships next month,” Pei says. “It’s a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product. It has no new screen, and it couldn’t have been an app.”

Pei is playing it characteristically coy. He’s dropping clues, and you can bet there will be more to come in the ensuing days and weeks up until the official launch of this mystery product.

Standalone AI devices are a burgeoning industry, even if they’re yet to result in a hugely compelling, must-have consumer product. Whether it be pins, pendants, glasses, headphones or tabletop devices, tech companies are flooding the market with new native AI devices. Some companies, such as OpenAI, are working on ideas behind closed doors, whereas others, such as AI note-taking experts Plaud, are already establishing a strong and loyal customer base.

British startup Nothing is predominantly known for its retro-inspired audio products and cool smartphones, around which the company is building a cult following as an alternative to more mainstream, generic phone companies. It’s more closely aligned with lifestyle and fashion brands than most of its tech brethren. In spite of this, it sounds like its first AI device will be more work than play.

Just like computers, AI will need to prove itself in the realm of productivity — the workplace — before it spills over into being truly useful and appreciated in our personal lives, writes Pei. And so, Nothing is building a tool for the workplace, albeit one with the company’s customary design-forward approach.

“We were taught that seriousness and beauty could not share a room,” says Pei. But he wants you to know that work tools can be beautiful, and he promises Nothing’s will be.

This is all very mysterious — perhaps more so because the image accompanying Pei’s post actually looks like it could be a snapshot of one of many different smartphones from the past decade or more. The simple black rectangle with one rounded corner looks distinctly unlike a Nothing device, and something a less imaginative tech company might produce.

We shouldn’t be fooled by this, though. Nothing has yet to bore us with a design, and it seems unlikely to start now — especially after Pei’s treatise on the subject. No doubt there will be more hints forthcoming, as Nothing gears up to persuade you that its products belong just as much in your office as at a warehouse rave in Berlin, and that its approach to AI is essential to your workflow above and beyond the offerings of its strait-laced competitors.

Coty Inc. (COTY +12.68%) reported first-quarter results that exceeded management's internal expectations for sales and adjusted EBITDA, despite a modest reported revenue decline of 1%. Management characterized the current period as a transition year focused on the Coty.Curated strategic framework, which prioritizes resources toward 10 core brands that represent the majority of segment revenues. The company reported a narrowing of like-for-like sales declines in its Consumer Beauty division and growth in its primary Prestige brands, particularly in the U.S. and China. Strategic focus remains on organizational simplification, debt reduction, and identifying fixed-cost savings to fund disciplined reinvestment in brand advocacy and influencer marketing.

Operator: Good morning, and good afternoon, everyone. My name is Tasha, and I'll be your conference operator today. Please note that on November 4, at approximately 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time or 10:30 p.m. Central European Time, Coty issued a press release and prepared remarks webcast, which can be found on its Investor Relations website. But could you explain what drove this slight miss? And you also provided the guidance for Q1, but not for Q2. Secondly, thank you very much for providing all the details on the performance of your 6 core Prestige brands and 4 core consumer brands.
