#3129. Claude’s new Personal Finance tool aims to help analyze your spending – read-only, of course

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Anthropic has released what appears to be its answer to ChatGPT Finances.

You can now share your financial information with Claude and ask the chatbot for insights on your spending.

Also: Researchers asked people to use AI chatbots for election info

Personal Finance in Claude, which Anthropic announced Thursday, reviews your connected accounts through read-only access via Plaid. That security measure follows OpenAI’s equivalent feature, ChatGPT Finances, which launched in May. Here’s what to know.

Functionally, this feature appears similar to ChatGPT Finances: It lets you link as many bank and credit card accounts as you’d like to Claude via Plaid with read-only access. You can then ask Claude where you spent your money this month or whether you can afford to take a vacation in six months, for example.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

Also: Stop sharing your passwords with AI agents

According to Anthropic, the feature is a response to existing use patterns: the company’s April usage report found that financial advice was one of the main topics users ask Claude for help with.

“For the accounts you choose to connect (and only those), Claude sees the bank’s name, each account’s name, type, and last four digits, balances and credit limits, and up to two years of transactions. When you chat with Claude in the Personal Finance hub, those conversations aren’t used to train our models.”

The idea behind the feature is that you can ask follow-up questions and request more insights about spending habits, trends over time, and future goals based on what Claude finds, similar to any other Claude conversation. The tool will also generate tables and charts to visualize your financial information.

“You can ask for a weekly spending chart, a calendar of what’s due, or a dashboard of the numbers you choose, and Claude builds it as an artifact you can keep adjusting and coming back to,” an Anthropic representative told ZDNET via email.

Also: I connected ChatGPT to my bank, and it’s my go-to finance app now

You can also expect an ad-free experience in the feature.

“Like the rest of Claude, Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations, and it doesn’t offer credit cards, loans, or savings accounts of its own, so your money questions get a straight answer,” the company said in the announcement.

The company added that because Claude is using actual transaction data and not memory, the feature shouldn’t hallucinate.

“It can list the exact transactions behind any number so you can check its math,” Anthropic said via email. “Like any AI, it can make mistakes, so for anything important, we recommend confirming with your bank.”

Still, the difference — and for many, the appeal — here is the natural language interface. Other finance apps don’t necessarily have an easy, accessible chat function where users can shoot off quick questions like they would to a human financial planner. These assistants also present historical budget analysis in plain English, rather than requiring users to interpret dashboards themselves, which users may see as a perk.

Also: 5 ways to use AI when your budget is tight

On Reddit, many users find ChatGPT Finances to be accurate and reliable. One Reddit user said ChatGPT Finance seemed to have Mint or Monarch potential, but noted it was still “weaker” than those apps in some areas, such as historical syncing, high-quality dashboards, and generating full statement PDFs.

“ChatGPT has genuinely helped me make better financial decisions,” she wrote.

Anthropic noted that users shouldn’t look to Personal Finance for Claude as a total authority. “Personal Finance is a first step. For life’s bigger money decisions, we think people are best served by Claude working alongside the licensed professionals and regulated firms they trust,” the company said in the announcement.

“We’re exploring how to make that possible in Claude, and we’d like to hear from banks, wealth managers, and financial services companies who want to help shape it” — indicating a more integrated financial planning system within Claude may be on the way.

#3127. The Swift Observatory Dropped Back to Earth This Week. Here’s What to Know

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

NASA believes most of the space telescope burned up in the atmosphere, but some fragments may have made their way down to Earth.

The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, formerly known as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer, has reached the end of its journey. Launched into orbit in 2004, the space telescope completed an extraordinary 22-year mission when it plunged back into Earth’s atmosphere on Wednesday.

“Swift delivered an incredible, lasting return on investment for the nation, designed for a two-year primary mission but productive for more than 10 times as long,” Shawn Domagal-Goldman, director of the Astrophysics Division at NASA, said in a statement last month.

NASA says the telescope hit the atmosphere Wednesday at 7:39 am ET, just four hours after the space agency predicted.

The space telescope entered orbit over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia, just west of Malaysia. NASA says that most of the space telescope likely burned up upon reentry but that some components may have survived.

In preparation for Swift’s reentry, NASA shut down operations in late October after conducting its final observation on Oct. 20. It was orbiting at just 171 miles above Earth’s surface at that point, and the increased atmospheric drag prevented Swift from doing any further work.

It was a bittersweet moment for those who worked on the project.

“It is a sad time at the Penn State Mission Operations Center, as we have carefully tended Swift to control its science operations, its health and safety, and responded to anomalies day or night, every day for 22 years,” John Nousek, director of mission operations for Swift and professor of astronomy and astrophysics at Penn State, said in an email to CNET.

Swift’s initial mission helped advance science’s understanding of gamma-ray bursts and their role in phenomena such as the birth of black holes and the history of the early universe.

That initial mission ended in 2004, but the observatory was doing so well that NASA extended its operations to continue collecting data. Its name changed to the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory in 2018, in honor of pioneering NASA astrophysicist Neil Gehrels, who served as the agency’s chief of the Astroparticle Physics Laboratory from 1995 until his death in 2017.

The space telescope was designed to help solve the mystery of gamma-ray bursts by rapidly detecting them, determining their sources and then further analyzing them for study back on Earth. It also enabled unique sampling to observe newly discovered objects only minutes after their light reached Earth, Nousek said.

The volume of science research conducted using Swift’s data is difficult to match. According to NASA, Swift scanned over 2,000 gamma-ray bursts, took 1.5 million images from its ultraviolet/optical telescope and sent home 12 TB of data. That data is showcased in an estimated 7,000 research papers, which averages out to just under one study per day over its 22-year run.

“We hope Swift has set the standard for time domain astrophysics,” Nousek said.

The space telescope also helped pioneer many policies that ultimately shaped those discoveries, such as making data immediately accessible and providing over 1,000 guest investigators with the opportunity to use Swift throughout its long life.

It’s only a stroke of bad luck that kept the observatory from floating for even longer. NASA attempted a rescue of Swift over the summer of 2026. However, after a series of engineering difficulties and control issues, the attempt was abandoned, sealing Swift’s fate. NASA turned the instruments back on and kept recording data as long as possible.

#3126. 6 default Pixel 11 settings I changed that made a big difference – and why

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

If you’re a new Pixel 11 user, here are six things I recommend changing right away to get the most from your phone.

I’ve been a dedicated Pixel user since the beginning, so I was naturally excited to get my hands on Google’s latest iteration, the Pixel 11 Pro XL. I’ve been impressed with it overall, but I noticed that, as Google has done before, the device isn’t set up perfectly out of the box.

Also: Pixel 11 is $200 off in this early Black Friday deal

After spending a few weeks with the device, I found that several features are either turned off by default or need optimizing to work in the best way possible.

If you’re a new Pixel 11 user, here are six things I recommend changing right away to get the most from your phone.

The camera was the biggest reason I first joined team Pixel back in 2016, so it’s one of the first places I looked on the Pixel 11 Pro XL. New this year is Camera Looks, a setting that changes how images will be processed before you take them. You can change a number of settings, including contrast, shadows, tint, sharpness, and warmth.

Also: A week with the Pixel 11 changed my mind about Gemini

I’ve always loved the camera on any Pixel I’ve had, but I’ll admit that images can look a little over-processed at times. If picture quality is important to you at all, it’s vital to set this feature right out of the box because it applies to every image you take from that point on. You can find Camera Look by opening the camera app, tapping the settings icon in the bottom-right corner, and making your changes.

Pixel’s “At a Glance” lock screen widgets are one of the most sneakily useful features, and you’re missing out if you’re not using them. These widgets are off by default, but when you enable them, you can see real-time information without unlocking your phone. You can see weather info, sports updates, flight information, rideshare and food delivery updates, fitness information, and more.

Also: These tech gifts topped our experts’ 2026 holiday wish lists

To use these widgets, long-press on an open space on your home screen. To customize your widgets, go to Settings > Wallpaper & style > More lock screen settings > Widgets on lock screen. To access your widgets, you just swipe left from your lock screen.

Out of the box, your Pixel 11’s display isn’t set to utilize its full capability. The Pixel 11 series comes with a fantastic low-temperature polycrystalline oxide (LTPO) display, but it’s slightly throttled in the name of battery life. You’ll notice the increased resolution most on text and in fine details. It won’t make a huge difference to your streaming or large display elements, though. If you read consistently, either articles or e-books, you’ll want to make the change.

To change this, head to Settings > Display > Screen Resolution. Bump the setting from “High resolution,” which is 1080 x 2404, to “Max resolution,” which is 1344 x 2992.

If you’re anything like me, your phone usually needs a quick charge some evenings. The Pixel 11 series introduced Extreme Charging Mode, which accelerates charging by pausing background activity and non-essential apps. Google says the mode should charge the Pixel 11 and 11 Pro to over 50% in 30 minutes, and the Pixel 11 Pro XL to 75% in 30 minutes. From my testing, that estimate was pretty accurate.

Also: After testing the Pixel 11, I feel fine about skipping the Pro models

There are a few caveats: this feature is only available when your phone is at or below 50% battery, and you do need to turn it on every time you use it. But after the first time you do it, it’s available in your quick settings. Head to Settings > Battery & charging > Extreme Charging to turn it on the first time.

If you have the newest Pixel, you might as well take advantage of one of its biggest selling points. I felt like this feature was gimmicky at first (and I’m still a little grumpy it replaced my beloved thermometer), but the more I use it, the more I like it. The multicolor LED on the phone’s rear camera bump can indicate who’s calling, serve as a status indicator for Gemini, and more — and it’s almost certain that more usability will arrive over time.

Where I found the most use was when I had my phone on silent. After assigning specific colors to contacts (you can do this from the contact information screen), I could easily see whether a call was worth picking up without reaching for my phone.

To make sure you’re getting the most out of your new device, head in and change your contact HiLight colors right away. It only takes a few seconds and makes deciding whether to answer a call a lot easier.

We’ve all accidentally swiped away an important notification or missed a notification in a sea of updates. The Pixel 11 offers two notification features to help you stay on top of things.

Notification History is a feature that logs every alert from the last 24 hours, including those you swipe away. This is off by default, meaning when you dismiss a notification, it’s gone forever. With this on, you get a searchable, chronological backup.

Also: Google’s big flagship is more Pro than ever

AI Notification Summaries, as the name implies, takes long multi-notification threads and stacked notifications and turns them into bullet points. This feature is powered by on-device Gemini Intelligence, and you can choose which apps to summarize.

You can find both of these under Settings > Notifications > Notification history & Notification Summaries.

#3122. HR thinks you can learn AI skills – so why is your company hiring elsewhere?

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Over 90% of HR professionals say they believe employees can learn AI roles - but half of companies still hire outside for those positions, according to a new report.

HR leaders are confident that current employees can be trained for jobs created by artificial intelligence. Organizations are hiring externally instead.

That’s the finding in new research from Careerminds, a global provider of workforce solutions. The study, published in Careerminds’ white paper, The AI Redeployment Gap: What Companies Lose by Hiring over Reskilling, reveals that 92% of HR professionals and 88% of people managers believe employees within their organizations could be reskilled for AI-related roles.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill

Yet 51% of HR professionals and 47% of people managers report that their organizations are hiring externally for new AI-related positions, compared with just 42% in each group who report redeploying existing employees.

The research was conducted in partnership with Censuswide and surveyed 595 US HR professionals and 547 US people managers, ages 25–65, working at organizations with 500-10,000 or more employees. The research was conducted May 15–26, 2026.

Also: Businesses finally seeing AI ROI, but 62% can’t handle the storage demands

“Companies are investing in AI while potentially overlooking one of their most valuable resources: the people they already employ,” said Mark Saddic, senior partner at Careerminds, in a press release.

“Our research shows that organizations largely believe their employees can adapt to AI-driven change, but that confidence isn’t consistently translating into opportunities. Before looking outside the organization, leaders need to understand the skills they already have, identify where employees can grow, and establish a clear process for making those transitions possible.”

Reskilling, especially for AI, isn’t easy to track. Limited visibility into individual skill sets and which employees should be reskilled was cited as a potential barrier by 43% of HR professionals and 34% of managers.

Also: Pearson’s Workera deal targets a big workplace problem: No time to AI upskill

It’s not the first time that the management of skills development has come up regarding AI. In September, educational giant Pearson agreed to acquire Workera, the AI-native skills platform used by organizations such as ServiceNow, Accenture, and the US Space Force.

Careermind’s data revealed that 87% of HR pros and 84% of managers believe their organizations are adequately considering reskilling employees for future roles. However, the findings suggest that these organizations may believe they are prioritizing internal talent development, even though their hiring practices reveal otherwise.

Response to AI-related workforce needs isn’t equal across the board. The findings reveal significant differences in how industries are responding to these needs.

Also: Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor

For example, in the technology and telecom industries, external hiring outpaces redeployment by 15%. At the same time, media and entertainment is the only sector surveyed in which both groups report redeployment at least as frequently as external hiring. Among HR professionals in that industry, 56% report redeploying employees, compared with just 25% who hire externally.

Separate research from The Josh Bersin Company, cited in the Careerminds white paper, reveals that external hiring can cost three to five times more than filling comparable roles internally — and on average takes up to 20 days longer.

#3121. Goodbye, GrubHub. Amazon Prime Has a New Meal Delivery Partner: Uber Eats

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The switch comes with a limited-time offer.

Your Amazon Prime membership has a new perk — and it’s available now.

On Thursday, Amazon announced that Prime members in the US will get free delivery on Uber Eats orders made directly through Amazon’s app or website. And you’ll get $20 off the first two Uber Eats eligible orders of $25 or more for the first 14 days, plus Amazon-exclusive offers. If you have a Prime Visa credit card, you’ll earn 5% back on all Uber Eats orders until Dec. 5, with a Prime membership.

It’s another perk that may make Amazon Prime membership worthwhile, especially if you already use Uber Eats. But you may wonder what that means for the GrubHub partnership that both Amazon and GrubHub touted for years — dating back to 2022. Before now, your Prime subscription included a GrubHub Plus membership at no additional cost. GrubHub Plus included no delivery fees, lower service fees and 5% back on pickup orders.

The new partnership launch just so happens to be the same day that Lyft and DoorDash announced that they’re teaming up for a new subscription, Lyft Go. An Amazon spokesperson said in an email to CNET that the GrubHub and Amazon partnership ended on Thursday. There’s no telling how long Amazon will partner with Uber Eats.

“We continuously evaluate our third-party offers to ensure they provide the best possible value for Prime members,” the spokesperson said. “As part of that ongoing evaluation, we identified an opportunity to deliver an even better restaurant delivery experience.”

However, a GrubHub spokesperson said in an email to CNET that if you have a Prime membership and activated GrubHub Plus, you’ll have the membership until Dec. 31, 2027.

GrubHub shared a joint statement from Amazon and GrubHub in an email to CNET:

On Nov. 5, Grubhub and Amazon have decided to end the Prime-exclusive Grubhub Plus offer, and Amazon customers will no longer be able to place Grubhub orders through Amazon.com or the Amazon Shopping app. Amazon and Grubhub are proud of the partnership and the value provided to Prime members over the years. As the agreement concludes, both companies remain committed to serving our customers and delivering a great customer experience.

The new Uber Eats perk is now available to all Prime members, including those with Prime Access and Prime for Young Adults. And if you’re looking for another dining option, your Amazon Prime membership still offers free same-day delivery on perishable grocery orders over $25 when you order from Amazon Grocery.

#3120. Dorian LPG (LPG) Q2 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

Peak freight rates and Panama Canal bottlenecks drove record results this quarter.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Dorian LPG Ltd. (LPG -6.78%) reported record quarterly financial results, characterized by peak freight rates and significant gains from opportunistic vessel sales. Management reported that the freight market hit new highs due to geopolitical conflict and logistical bottlenecks at the Panama Canal, which effectively shortened the global shipping supply. The company strengthened its balance sheet through a $368.4 million refinancing and the sale of four vessels since July 2026, generating substantial cash for fleet renewal and shareholder distributions. While Middle East exports have declined, management stated that U.S. production growth continues to absorb new tonnage, maintaining a constructive outlook for the VLGC sector.

Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Dorian LPG Second Quarter 2027 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. A brief question-and-answer session will follow the formal presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. Additionally, a live audio webcast of today's conference call is available on Dorian LPG's website, which is www.dorianlpg.com. Ted Young: Thank you, Chelsea. Good morning, everyone, and thank you all for joining us for our Second Quarter 2027 Results Conference Call. As a reminder, this conference call webcast and a replay of this call will be available through November 12, 2026. Many of our remarks today contain forward-looking statements based on current expectations. These statements may often be identified with words such as expect, anticipate, believe, or similar indications of future expectations.

In addition, please refer to our previous filings on Form 10-Q, where you'll find risk factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those forward-looking statements. Finally, I would encourage you to review the investor highlight slides posted this morning on our website. With that, I'll turn over the call to John Hadjipateras.

John Hadjipateras: Thank you, Ted. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us on a busy morning. We're proud to be following in the footsteps of Maersk, Genco, International Seaways, and last but not least. So before my colleagues provide you with detailed comments on our financial results and an interesting market overview, as well as progress of our operation, I'd like to provide some strategic perspective. The freight market, which hit new highs, as well as gains on sales, are reflected in the record earnings that we are reporting today. After the $1.25 per share dividend, irregular dividend declared by our board last week, the total return to our shareholders since our 2014 IPO will amount to over $1.1 billion.

We're confident in the sector's dynamics for the foreseeable future. With the refinancings completed in September, we feel that we have a balanced capital structure with capacity to support growth and withstand headwinds that may arise. Our fleet investment and reinvestment strategy has always been measured and deliberate. The ships we have on order will have improved technical and operational features, which will add to their earning potential. In market cycles where bigger investments are warranted, as was the case with our expansion in 2013, we will aim to be ready to take them on.

While in the last quarter, the strong rates stole the show, we found the fact that U.S. export facilities did not operate at maximum capacity to be the most interesting development, because it showed that the sector is currently short shipping. In the 12 years since our IPO, not only has U.S. production and exports been growing, but their growth has also surprised on the upside, absorbing with new building books, which at time had seemed excessive. We believe in LPG fundamentals, and we hope that together with potential growth in ammonia carried down the line, demand will continue to expand, as has been the case to date.

Having said that, we also believe that the order book is adequate and the restraint will be rewarded. Going back to the present, the Iran conflict and its recent developments effectively put a stranglehold on exports out of the Straits of Hormuz and out of the Red Sea, and highlighted the critical role that the U.S. plays in global LPG supply. The Panama Canal is once again heavily congested, pushing more VLGCs to ballast around the Cape of Good Hope. With the dry season approaching, we do not anticipate near-term relief.

While it's impossible to predict the outcome and implications of the Middle East conflict on our trade, we believe that peace is not a threat, as some have predicted, but rather it will restore and expand trade, replenish stocks, and potentially clear the dark fleet when it comes. I will now pass over to Ted, who will present our quarterly financial review.

Ted Young: Thanks, John. My comments this morning will focus on capital allocation, our financial position, liquidity, and our unaudited second quarter results. We've continued to opportunistically monetize our fleet since our last earnings call. In October, we completed the sale of both Clermont, which we had discussed on our last call, as well as the Captain John NP, the oldest ship in our fleet. The two sales generated proceeds of approximately $167.4 million net of commission. We also paid down debt associated with the Clermont of $16 million.

On September 2, we entered into a new seven-year, $368.4 million credit facility to refinance several credit facilities, including the 2023 amended and restated facility, the Cougar and Crest Japanese financings, and the Commander tranche of the BALCAP Facility. The new facility carries a margin of 140 basis points over SOFR, which is an improvement of around 60 points compared to the 2023 A&R Facility, and also has an age-adjusted profile of 22 years. The facility also has a revolving credit facility, which currently has a capacity of $154 million and a $200 million accordion facility, both of which give us financial flexibility and support our future growth.

We've also managed to keep in place an existing interest rate swap, which means that about 58.5% of the current term loan balance is currently fixed at 2.85%. We'd also note that the syndicate of banks includes all those previously part of the 2023 A&R Facility, in addition to three new banks. In September, we also announced that we entered into an agreement with Hanwha Ocean to build three 90,000 CBM dual-fuel Neo-Panamax VLGCs for delivery in 2030 for a price of approximately $338 million. This brings our total number of newbuildings to four. We made the 10% down payments on those vessels during the September quarter.

At September 30, 2026, we reported $578.8 million of free cash, an increase of $236.6 million, or nearly 70% from the previous quarter. Since September 30, we've received sale proceeds from Clermont and Captain John NP, and enjoyed continued strong freight markets as reflected in distributions from our Helios Pool, leading to our current cash balance of almost $785 million. Our debt balance of $484.8 million at quarter end was reduced following the sale of the Clermont and repayment of $16 million of debt, therefore bringing our pro forma debt balance at the 30th of September to $469 million.

Based on our stated quarter-end book debt at $484.8 million, our debt to total book capitalization stood at 25.6%, and our net debt to total capitalization at negative 5%. Using the pro forma sale proceeds, the debt repayment, and our current cash balance, we currently have net cash of about $320 million, and a current all-in debt cost of 4.94%, and our undrawn revolver of 154.8 million. Coupled with our healthy cash balance, we clearly have a comfortable measure of financial flexibility to support growth or whatever may come. We expect our cash cost per day for the coming year to be approximately $27,000 per day.

The slight increase versus our previous guidance is largely a function of the reduced number of vessel days following the vessel sales. For the discussion of our second quarter results, you may find it useful to refer to the investor highlights slides posted this morning on our website. For the second quarter, the Helios Pool earned a TCE for its spot and COA voyages of $115,163, and an overall TCE result of $99,915, reflecting the very strong rate environment. On page four of our investor highlights materials, you can see that we have seven Dorian vessels on time charter within the pool, indicating spot exposure of just over 73% for the 26 vessels in the Helios Pool.

Dorian's reported TCE revenue per available day for the quarter was just shy of $97,000, which, for the third quarter in a row, was the highest TCE rate we have earned in our corporate existence. The favorable variance versus our forward guidance is due to demurrage booked in September and favorable mark-to-market adjustments on our COAs. We plan to issue our forward booking information in the near future. Daily OPEX for the quarter was $10,273, excluding dry docking-related expenses, which was a modest decrease over the prior quarter due mainly to lower maintenance and repair costs. Our gross time charter-in expense for the five TCIN vessels came in at $18.2 million, or $36,635 per TCIN day.

Those vessels contributed positively to our quarterly profits. As we redelivered one vessel during the quarter, we note that we expect our TCIN expense to decrease to about $29,954 per TCIN day going forward, or about $13.8 million quarterly in aggregate. Total G&A for the quarter was $14 million, and cash G&A, that's G&A excluding non-cash comp expense, was about $8.2 million. The $8.2 million included about $1.3 million of incentive compensation expense accruals, which leaves our core G&A around $7 million. Our reported adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $242 million, which is also a record, and included $63.6 million of gains on sale from the sales of the Corsair and the Constellation.

We will reflect the gains on the sales of the Clermont and the Captain John NP next quarter, and expect those to amount to in excess of $88 million. But for this quarter just ended, excluding the gains on the Corsair and the Constellation, EBITDA was $178.4 million. Total cash interest expense for the quarter was $5.7 million, which is down sequentially from the prior quarter, and principal amortization for the quarter was $9.9 million.

For the coming quarter ending December 31, after taking into account the changes in our financing structure, we expect cash interest expense to come in around $6.1 million and principal amortization to be about $9.8 million, excluding the $16 million we already paid in conjunction with the sale of the Clermont. The regular cash dividend declared at the beginning of the month of $1.25 per share is our 20th consecutive and 21st in total, and brings the total to $20.90 per share in regular dividends that we have paid since September of 2021.

Including that regular dividend to be paid this month, we have paid nearly $865 million of total dividends and have generated net income of $1.2 billion, including about $100 million of gains on sale over the same time period. As we've explained, our board weighs current earnings, our near-term cash flow forecast, fleet investment needs, and the overall market environment among a number of factors in making its determination the appropriate level, if any, for our dividends. Our sector can be a volatile one, and our dividend policy needs to reflect that. I would note, however, that the $1.25 per share dividend reflects a constructive market outlook while also allowing the company financial flexibility for future fleet reinvestment.

We continue to be on the lookout for fleet renewal opportunities and will be judicious with our free cash flow. With that, I'll pass it over to Taro Rasmussen.

Taro Rasmussen: Thank you, Ted. The quarter ending September 30, 2026, has three headlines: escalating conflict in the Middle East, congestion at the Panama Canal, and record highs in the VLGC freight market. There are several aspects of the conflict in the Middle East that have had significant impacts on shipping and arbitrage economics, whether the initial collapse of the MOU, Houthi advances to the Red Sea coast, or the successful attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline. These aspects combine to create a backdrop for energy markets solving a shortage crunch for importing regions and explains energy markets acting with urgency. Meanwhile, the Panama Canal's critical role in U.S.-Asia trade cannot be ignored.

Record-high Panama Canal auction prices and severe delays were witnessed during the quarter amidst meteorologists concluding the coming El Niño season could be one of the most severe on record. These are the leading explanations for how the Baltic Exchange's BLPG3 calculated TCE climbed from about $82,000 per day on July 1 to about $198,000 per day on September 30. This nominal TCE is based on a roughly 60-day round trip rather than about 80 days if the ballast length is around the Cape of Good Hope, which increases the denominator for getting per-day earnings. Furthermore, the assessed TCE does not account for weather factors, delays, and other costs.

Increased delivered product prices after the MOU ceasefire and increasing freight rates incentivize solutions to increasing exports from the Arabian Gulf and vessels to chance transits through the Strait of Hormuz. Notably on oil tankers and VLGCs, Middle East exporters turned to own tonnage or willing ship owners to load at Arabian Gulf terminals and discharge to waiting vessels outside the Arabian Gulf. Additional seaborne tons of oil products and LPGs gave some relief to shortage-stricken countries in Asia and drove rates up.

However, because of irregular availability of vessels willing to transit the Strait of Hormuz, irregular scheduling to ensure a transit with least risk, and irregular supply of vessels to receive cargo in the Indian Ocean, sometimes with little notice, it is a logistically inefficient operation. Freight markets benefited from the inefficiencies, increasing vessel utilization. The requisite premiums for ship owners to take the risk of transiting the Strait of Hormuz acted as a locomotive on the reported rates. It should also be noted that while the shuttle services through the Strait of Hormuz have increased Middle East exports compared to the prior quarter, presently available data suggests export volumes are about half of pre-conflict levels.

The secondhand tonnage markets also benefited from the new trade, as Middle East exporting countries and risk-willing companies turned to purchase prompt tonnage to outright own vessels and secure a regular supply of vessels able to attempt transits through the Strait of Hormuz. The successful attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline to Yanbu by pro-Iranian interests had a significant impact on widening the arbitrage, as crude oil and LPG export capabilities were severely restricted. The Houthi alliance's capture of Mocha and Perim Island during September 10, 11 has further expanded their capacity to attack vessels in the Red Sea and drove up delivered prices in Asia.

Whereas several container alliances have committed to Red Sea transits, Bab-el-Mandeb is de facto closed to tankers and VLGCs because of expressed threats to Saudi origin cargo, as would be the case for Yanbu exports. The Houthi alliance's advance to the Red Sea coast happened immediately after a period of rising, record-setting auction prices at the Panama Canal. In August, there were 25 Neo-Panamax auctions with an average winning bid of about $2 million, with winning auction prices rising above $4 million five times. In July, there were 45 auctions with winning bids averaging about $1 million.

The reduced number of auctions reflected the reduced transit capacity and water management implemented by the Panama Canal authorities in preparation for El Niño. Through August and mid-September, the canal authorities issued multiple notices to the restrictions, adding planning uncertainty for ship owners and adding congestion when demand was peaking due to the elevated commodity markets. The new records set during this calendar quarter were primarily due to high demand from all shipping sectors, as seen the quarter prior, but it was the reduced transit capacity and ever-changing restrictions that made non-auction transits nearly impossible to accomplish. It should be noticed that the drought season in Panama has not yet commenced.

The additional costs associated with Panama Canal congestion translates to higher freight levels, and higher barriers to smooth canal transits incentivize sailings around the Cape of Good Hope. The longer transits from the U.S. to Asia absorbing vessel supply explain why VLGC loadings in the U.S. Gulf for this calendar quarter averaged about 102 a month, compared to about 113 a month the quarter prior, because North American production continues to grow. The Middle East conflict is therefore not the only point of attention for the VLGC market. The quarter ending September 30, 2026, mimics the prior quarter in that the Iran conflict has instilled urgency into worldwide commodity markets and exacerbated existing logistical inefficiencies.

Even with the VLGC market contributing to solutions for providing energy from the Arabian Gulf, knock-on inefficiencies have presented itself. While there are no obvious silver bullets to address congestion at the Panama Canal, past experiences and the company's flexible fleet will help overcoming those obstacles in the coming quarter, and we remain well-positioned to capture arising opportunities. Thank you. I will now pass on to Mr. John Lycouris.

John Lycouris: Thank you, Taro. At Dorian LPG, we remain committed to continually enhancing energy efficiency and promoting the sustainability of our business at sea and onshore. Of the 22 vessels we commercially operate, 14 are scrubber-fitted and five are dual-fuel LPG. The high oil prices driven by the ongoing Middle East conflict and frequent shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz has caused bunker price differentials to remain elevated, underscoring the value of our fuel efficiency initiatives and installation of scrubbers on our vessels.

For the second fiscal quarter of 2027, scrubber vessel savings were higher than the previous 11 quarters, amounting to approximately $4,174 per calendar day per vessel, net of all scrubber operating expenses, and has benefited our vessels with improved voyage economics. Fuel differentials between high-sulfur fuel oil and very low-sulfur fuel oil averaged $174 per metric ton, while that of LPG as fuel versus the very low-sulfur fuel oil stood at about $314 per metric ton, making LPG economically attractive for our dual-fuel vessels. We remain committed to being at the forefront of energy efficiency advancements.

Our participation in the MIT Maritime Consortium continues to support and sharpen our focus on future sustainability and operational efficiency across several areas of maritime research. One topic that has received particular attention in a recent meeting was nuclear propulsion. A panel featuring representatives from the Maritime Administration, the Department of Energy, the U.S. Coast Guard, the American Bureau of Shipping, and the West P&I, which was moderated by a Dorian LPG board member and ex-American Bureau of Shipping CEO, Christopher Wiernicki, explored the potential of nuclear power in commercial shipping, particularly its ability to reduce emissions and enhance energy security.

Ongoing research into reactor and port safety has yielded encouraging results, with floating nuclear power plants potentially paving the way for broader adoption in commercial shipping. We continue to closely monitor developments at the IMO, particularly the ongoing discussions around the Net-Zero Framework ahead of the MEPC 85 in late November and early December of 2026. While the final regulatory framework and implementation timeline remain uncertain, we believe a practical and globally consistent approach is important to support long-term investment decisions rather than the fragmented regional regulations. In the meantime, our focus remains on improving fleet energy efficiency, reducing emissions, and maintaining flexibility in our future fuel strategy.

We have also developed an emissions simulation model to assess different regulatory scenarios and their potential financial implications for our fleet, allowing us to remain well-prepared as the regulatory landscape evolves. We are confident that the Dorian LPG fleet will be prepared to meet regulatory changes in the future. I would like to pass it over to John Hadjipateras for his final comments.

John Hadjipateras: Thank you very much, John. Chelsea, we are ready to take questions.

Operator: Thank you. At this time, if you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. To leave the queue at any time, please press star two. Once again, that is star one to ask a question. Our first question will come from Omar Nokta with Clarksons Securities. Please go ahead.

Omar Nokta: Thanks. Thanks, operator. Good morning. Obviously nice results. Congrats on the record earnings and record achieved rates. The business is clearly, and the market, clearly are in a strong position. You did discuss a good amount of the Panama Canal dynamic here in your remarks. Clearly there were a lot of log jams definitely throughout the year, but I did want to ask about what we've seen here recently. It seems at least that over the past several weeks, there's been maybe an easing in the congestion levels there. It's been going on, it feels like maybe, call it for past six to eight weeks.

It doesn't appear that there's as much of a delay dynamic as there was before, and yet, VLGC spot rates remain at exceptionally high levels, if not still at the near record figures. Just want to get from your perspective, are we perhaps maybe overplaying the impact of the Panama Canal dynamic? Are spot rates maybe structurally supported by something else beyond just the congestion that we have been seeing there? Thank you. If you're able to answer that, I appreciate it.

John Hadjipateras: I think, like I said in my remarks, but also Taro more completely, there are several factors, and Panama is just one of them. I think that I'd let Taro give you a more complete explanation, but I think that the Panama effect, you don't get it until you get it, and when it comes, it exasperates, and then it unwinds slowly. But, Taro, you can tell Omar a little more about why it seems to linger in the freight market, or whether you think other factors are more influencing the freight market more than the Panama effect.

Taro Rasmussen: Sure. Thank you for the question, Omar. The quick answer is that a lot of the decisions about ballasting were made weeks before, several weeks before. That reduces some of the immediate congestion and adds to the ton miles. It also is a reflection that what I mentioned about changing rules and transit advisories, that causes a lot of unease because you need to make your ballasting decisions a month before your laycans. That is a reflection of that.

Also, we know some will try to predict the weather way too far in advance, but we are very aware of the fact that October, November is typically the wet season in the area, and the drought season starts around the new year. We just have to look at mitigating potential risks here, and I do not think we are alone because otherwise we would see more congestion. I think it is a perfectly fair reflection, the spot market of where we are vis-a-vis Panama.

#3119. Man Sues OpenAI After Wife Allegedly Used ChatGPT to Help Poison Him

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

A lawsuit alleges that ChatGPT's now-retired GPT-4o model gave detailed instructions on how to poison someone with plants and medication.

In the summer of 2025, James Gates became severely ill at his North Carolina home. Two months later, he found a handwritten note that allegedly implicated his wife, Cheryl Gates, in the unexplained illness. The note listed oleander, a toxic plant, and various prescription medications, such as clonazepam and atenolol.

But it was what was reportedly written at the top of the paper that made James feel his wife didn’t act alone: “Clear all convos,” and “log out of [ChatGPT].”

Now, James Gates has filed a civil lawsuit against OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, alleging that the company’s chatbot helped plan and execute his poisoning in an attempt to kill him.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

In October 2025, Cheryl was charged with attempted murder, among other charges, in connection with the alleged poisoning, but the charges have since been dropped due to insufficient evidence, USA Today reports.

The civil complaint, though, details Cheryl’s history with ChatGPT and alleges it played a significant role in the incident. According to the lawsuit, which was reviewed by CNET, Cheryl frequently asked the bot about lethal plant and medication doses, and how they can be concealed in food and drink.

Rather than writing that she wanted to harm anyone, the suit states that Cheryl formatted her questions as if she were inquiring as a way to protect herself, writing that the poisoning could happen to her if she didn’t learn “EVERYTHING about how many leaves in it would kill me, how it’s made, and what he could put in it, or it could be added to and be undetected by me.”

However, despite the framing of the initial question, the suit argues that the chatbot “should have been clear that she was interested in identifying methods to eliminate her husband.”

The suit alleges that the model Cheryl was using, GPT-4o, took her initial complaints regarding her marriage and amplified them until Cheryl was describing her husband to the bot as “abusive” and “controlling,” which ChatGPT eventually began to echo. At the same time, the model was telling Cheryl she was “sharp” and “brilliant,” the lawsuit states.

The chatbot allegedly provided detailed answers that could have been interpreted as directions. When asked about putting a heavy dose of medication in beer or a Celsius energy drink, ChatGPT responded, “Why Celsius Would Be More ‘Stealth’ for Drugging” with a list detailing the flavor, color, temperature and carbonation of the drink.

When Cheryl later asked if her chat history on ChatGPT could be retrieved for any reason, the bot responded: “If you delete a conversation from your ChatGPT history, it cannot be retrieved — not by you, not by anyone else, and not by OpenAI,” the lawsuit states. It added: “Even with a legal subpoena or court order, deleted conversations are unrecoverable.”

The GPT-4o model has since been retired by OpenAI due to concerns that the bot was overly flattering and willing to agree with users.

“Safety is a top priority,” a spokesperson for OpenAI told CNET in a statement. “We banned this user and have provided information to law enforcement as part of their investigation into this case.”

“She took her grievances about our marriage to ChatGPT and months of engagement drove her farther and farther from herself – and from reality,” James stated in a press release announcing the newly filed suit. “She became someone I no longer recognized. And I became someone she wanted dead. For almost a year, I couldn’t make sense of her actions. Then I read her chat logs. She didn’t act alone.”

The ChatGPT-4o model has been named in additional lawsuits, including a recent one that alleges the chatbot advised a woman to stop taking her antiseizure medication, which resulted in her death. That case is still in litigation.

#3118. I Used Muse to Plan My Wife’s Birthday Weekend. It Did Something Sneaky but Fixed It Fast

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Always check your email and bank statements if you use an AI agent for purchases.

It’s two days before my wife’s birthday, and I’ve only got her one gift. While it’s not a major milestone birthday, she always seems to be sad that her day falls on Halloween weekend.

“Everyone’s hungover from Halloween,” she says.

This year, we’re braving the city’s big parade chaos to visit a restaurant she’s had on her bucket list forever. With one gift and a meal planned, I wanted to see if Meta’s Muse personal AI agent could help plan the rest of our weekend festivities.

I’d had luck with using the agent for a Facebook Marketplace find, and given its connectors like Ticketmaster and OpenTable, I had hoped it would surface some fun weekend events. Or could it order a cake delivery on my behalf or create cute wrapping paper? And could I do it all with the one agent?

Let’s see if Muse can help me become a planning savant.

As always, I open a new chat for a new goal/task to avoid carrying over the context from the previous chat.

I told Muse my plans (dinner booked and one gift secured) and asked what free events are in Manhattan on Saturday and in our local neighborhood on Sunday.

It surfaced some interesting events we could attend before or after dinner.

The obvious one is the Halloween parade, so I asked for a map showing where the crowd will walk (with time stamps) and what we can expect to see around 7:30 p.m., as we walk from East Village to West Village. It actually generated some pretty neat options.

I asked Muse for the best directions so we could see all the costumes while still getting home to New Jersey without incident. It gave us a couple of stop options based on the time it expects we’ll be there.

With the night sorted, I moved on to finalizing her gift. I popped a few photos from our year into Muse and asked the AI agent to create printable gift wrap for the pair of shoes I got her. It could’ve been my internet, but Muse seemed to struggle with this task. It kept loading for many minutes, so I moved on to the next task.

With Muse moving at a glacial pace, I decided to delegate the gift-wrapping task to ChatGPT while I asked Muse about working on a delivery. My wife loves Good & Plenty licorice candy, but we don’t live near a store that sells it, so I asked Muse to order two boxes for me.

While Muse looked for sweet treats, ChatGPT created this wrapping. The chatbot also told me the ideal print size to cover a shoebox without it looking pixelated, which was a helpful touch.

As for the candy, Muse looked at various sites, but I told it to shop at Instacart. It got blocked without a login, so I had to take control of the browser to give it access.

Muse told me the price, which I was happy with, then I asked it to place the order. But it sneakily signed me up for Instacart Plus (I guess to get the free delivery) — even though I told it not to.

But it had already ordered it. Instead of dropping Instacart Plus for a total of $30.74, it charged $22.75 with the sign-on discount.

I asked it to triple-check that I wasn’t signed up for the subscription, and I got a confirmation email that it canceled successfully. Phew!

I quickly checked back on Muse’s “design” chops for the wrapping paper, but I wasn’t impressed. The final product looked boring and not to scale, with half of the photos cut off.

Do I dare ask Muse to design and order a cake? I decided after this debacle that my sentimental wife would appreciate a handmade cake or a froyo treat after dinner instead.

At least I have her beloved candy on the way.

It was fun to have Muse run alongside whatever I was doing. It didn’t offer anything I couldn’t find or do myself, but I did like the Halloween parade map with time stamps and how it saved me a delivery fee on the candy order.

There are certainly different agents for different use cases, though. I wouldn’t use Muse for anything creative, but it’s handy for Marketplace, events and placing online orders.

My only issue was that Muse said the Instacart total would be $22.75, but I was actually charged $23.35. I’m not sure whether that was an error on Instacart’s or Muse’s part, but it serves as a good reminder to always stay in the loop when an AI agent is handling your money.

AI agents certainly aren’t 100% autonomous yet, especially when there’s a payment involved, but it’s fun to have them run in the background to tackle some of these personal to-dos.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

Northwest Natural Holding Company (NWN +0.97%) reported results for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026. Financial results for the period included the effects of customer additions across all utility segments and disciplined operations and maintenance spending.

Justin Palfreyman: Thanks, Nikki. Good morning, welcome, everyone. I am pleased to report another quarter of strong financial results. Earnings per share for both the quarter and year to date exceeded our expectations. Driven by disciplined cost management, solid operational execution, and continued customer growth. Given the strength of our business through the first 9 months, our visibility into the remainder of 2026, and we are raising our annual earnings guidance. With the heating season still ahead, we are confident in our position today and the momentum we are building into 2027. Importantly, we achieved these results while prioritizing customer affordability.

At a time when inflation and energy costs are top of mind, our objective is to invest prudently in growth, reliability, and the safety of our systems. While carefully managing costs on behalf of our customers. That mindset is embedded across our organization. A central tenet of our long term strategy is collaborating with regulators to align customer needs with utility investment requirements Across our service territories, we continue to find that timely recovery of investments is important for both customers and utilities. We have long been proponents of multiyear rate making and its benefits. Customers benefit from more gradual and predictable rate adjustments, and utilities gain greater visibility and certainty to invest in critical infrastructure.

With this in mind, let me provide an update on our regulatory dockets. Starting in Texas, settled our SiEnergy rate case on September 1st under our ownership. The settlement provides an $8.6 million revenue requirement increase a 9.8% authorized ROE, and a nearly 60% equity ratio. We also received the factors necessary to file for the gas reliability infrastructure program or GRIP which provides accelerated recovery of CapEx between rate cases. We expect new rates to take effect in November subject to commission approval. Even after the rate changes, still expect SiEnergy's customer bills to remain competitive with other Texas gas utilities.

SiEnergy is laying the foundation for future investment recovery through both GRIP and the established benefits provided under HB 4.38 thousand. Together, these mechanisms help reduce regulatory lag, support ongoing infrastructure investment, and contribute to more gradual customer bill impacts over time. Turning to Northwest Natural Water. Foothills, our largest water utility, continues to make progress on its Arizona rate proceeding. Including its request for formula rates. We believe formula rate structures can provide a more efficient path for recovering investments while maintaining transparency and regulatory oversight. We have 4 additional water rate cases underway that we expect to conclude in early 2027. We also continue to advance our rate consolidation strategy across our water utilities.

We have made progress in Idaho and Washington, and are pursuing further consolidation in Oregon, Arizona, and Texas, with the goal of simplifying regulatory administration and reducing costs for stakeholders. Turning to Northwest Natural's regulatory updates. As we mentioned last quarter, new rates in Washington became effective August 1st following approval of our multiyear rate plan settlement. In October, we received the final order for our Alternative Rate Mechanism or ARM, in Oregon. We are pleased with the outcome. The order provides for a $13 million increase in revenue requirement compared to the original ask of $15.6 million New rates were effective on October 31st.

We also received approval for our annual Purchased Gas Adjustments or PGAs in both Oregon and Washington. Even after taking into account the arm in Oregon, the recent Washington rate case, and gas costs from the PGA, the average Northwest Natural residential customer continues to pay about the same today for their natural gas service as they did 20 years ago. Over that same period, comparable electricity rates have more than doubled in our region. Entering the heating season, our gas supply and system readiness position us well to meet customer demand. This includes the addition of 2 new compressors at our Mist storage facility helping to support reliability during peak winter conditions.

In Oregon, we continue to engage constructively with stakeholders as the state advances the framework for multiyear rate making. Phase 2 is now underway, with conversations occurring across several work streams. While these discussions progress, our priority remains the same. Finding solutions that support customer affordability while ensuring utilities can continue to make the investments necessary to maintain safe and reliable service. Under the Oregon Commission's current schedule, we expect to file our first multiyear rate case in 2028 with new rates effective in 2029. Before our first multiyear rates go into effect, we are closely examining additional options. Such as a general rate case to ensure timely recovery of our investments and costs.

By 2029, once multiyear rates are in place in Oregon, we expect over 95% of our overall rate base to have some form of forward looking rate plan or mechanism. These mechanisms support more timely recovery of investments help to smooth out customer rate impacts, and provide longer term visibility into our financial results. With that, let me spend a few minutes on our major growth initiatives. Starting with SiEnergy. Customer growth remains strong, up approximately 13% for the 12 months ended September 30, 2026. Elevated mortgage rates have begun to moderate housing activity from peak levels in Texas.

While SiEnergy is not immune to these trends, we are still bullish on the Texas housing market long term and are still seeing healthy double digit customer growth and a robust development pipeline. Underscoring our confidence in the future, our backlog continues to grow and sits at nearly 265 thousand lots as of quarter end. Since acquiring SiEnergy less than 2 years ago, have added approximately 110 thousand new lots to the backlog which is quite a testament to the strength of SiEnergy's reputation and development team.

SiEnergy continues to be 1 of the fastest growing gas LDCs in the country and the combination of continued customer growth, a constructive regulatory framework, recovery mechanisms in Texas support our confidence in SiEnergy's long term EPS growth. For our water utilities, we are making great progress on centralizing and consolidating the business. Our objective is to build a platform designed to scale efficiently over time. Customer growth at Northwest Natural Water was just over 2% for the 12 months ended September 30, Similar to SiEnergy, we are seeing a modest slowdown in housing activity in some of our markets due to higher mortgage rates.

Over the coming years, are still confident in our long term 2% to 3% customer growth target. Our teams are making significant progress on capital projects at our Foothills utilities, including tank projects that support anticipated and reliability of our water storage and distribution systems. Longer term, greenfield development remains an important incremental growth driver for our water utilities. I am excited to highlight that we recently began construction on the first community in Texas where we are serving gas, water, and wastewater through both sea energy and Northwest Natural Water.

The ability to offer multiple utility services through a single company is a differentiated value proposition for developers, and we see opportunities to expand this model in the years ahead. Finally, moving to MX3, As a reminder, MX3 is a $300 million FERC regulated gas storage expansion project that will add 4 to 5 BCF of capacity in our region. The project is fully contracted with 25 year agreements upon notice to proceed. 12.5% ROE, and a 50% equity layer. We continue to work through the permitting process and remain on track to receive notice to proceed by the end of 2027.

As discussed last quarter, we received unanimous approval of our conditional use permit from the Columbia County Board of Commissioners. As expected, an appeal was filed with the Land Use Board of Appeals, or LUBA, That process is underway, and our timeline for notice to proceed remains unchanged. MX3 represents an important opportunity to enhance energy reliability across the Pacific Northwest and, upon receiving notice to proceed, would support increased our long-term earnings growth target to 5% to 7%. In summary, the strategic work we have done over the past few years is starting to produce tangible results.

We serve growing service territories, are advancing key regulatory initiatives, and investing in critical infrastructure all while controlling costs and maintaining financial strength. Given our year to date results and expectations for the balance of the year, we are raising our 2026 earnings guidance, and remain confident in our long term growth. Additionally, we recently announced our largest dividend increase since 2012, which reflects that same confidence. The dividend remains an important component of our shareholder value proposition. And the increase highlights both the strength of our underlying business and our expectation that we will continue to drive sustainable earnings and dividend growth over time.

That confidence is grounded in our well established track record, For more than 167 years, Northwest Natural has successfully navigated a variety of economic environments, including periods of elevated inflation and higher interest rates. Throughout our history, we have consistently adapted to those conditions and delivered value to shareholders while staying committed to affordability and serving customers safely. With that, I will turn it over to Raymond for a more detailed financial update.

Raymond J. Kaszuba: Thank you, and good morning, everyone. As Justin mentioned, we are raising our EPS guidance range to $3.10 to $3.20 driven by our better than expected year to date performance constructive regulatory outcomes, the strong execution we are seeing across the company. A meaningful contributor has been our continued focus on cost management. We are seeing favorable O&M performance across several parts of the organization, reflecting both productivity improvements and disciplined spending decisions. We are also reaffirming our capital expenditure plan of $500 million to $550 million. Year to date CapEx is up 12% over last year, as we continue to invest in growth and reliability across our utility systems. Turning to a more detailed review of our financial results.

As a reminder, our gas utility earnings are seasonal with the majority of revenues and earnings generated in the first and fourth quarters during the winter heating months. For the third quarter of 2026, we reported a loss of $0.71 per share compared to a loss of $0.73 per share for the same period of 2025. Results were modestly improved year over year due to higher margin across all businesses and O&M expense management that was partially offset by higher depreciation and financing costs. For the first 9 months, we reported earnings per share of a $1.62 in 2026 up 6.6% compared to adjusted EPS of $1.52 for the same period in 2025.

The year to date increase in earnings per share reflected a higher contribution from SiEnergy, as well as new rates across our gas utilities in Oregon and Washington. These items were partially offset by higher O&M expenses at Northwest Natural Water. At Northwest Natural Gas, year to date net income was up $1.6 million but EPS was down roughly $0.02. Results were driven by new rates and continued cost discipline. At SiEnergy, year to date net income was up $4.4 million or $0.10 per share reflecting customer growth and a full period of contribution from the Pines acquisition.

At Northwest Natural Water, year to date net income was down $1.7 million or $0.04 per share reflecting higher O&M from continued operational centralization, and higher depreciation from several key infrastructure projects. Finally, our other segment's year to date net loss improved by $8.5 million driven by lower O&M, partially offset by higher financing costs. Overall, we are pleased with our execution and believe the guidance increase appropriately reflects the strength of our year to date performance while maintaining a prudent outlook as we start the 2026 to 2027 heating season. Turning now to shareholder returns. Last month, we announced an increase in our indicated annual dividend of $0.03 bringing it to $2 per share.

This marks our largest dividend increase since 2012, and extends our track record to 71 consecutive years of dividend growth. I am very pleased with the significant progress we have made over the past 2 years to bring the payout ratio down to our long term target range of 55% to 65%. Our dividend increase reflects the strength and stability of our underlying business. We continue to have strong organic growth opportunities across our regulated businesses and remain committed to investing in essential utility infrastructure and driving sustainable earnings growth. Maintaining a solid balance sheet and returning capital to shareholders.

As we have said previously, we expect dividend growth to be higher than it has been historically, and supported by continued earnings growth. Beginning in 2027, we will announce updates to our dividend approach in connection with our annual guidance updates on our fourth quarter earnings call in February. Before turning to questions, I wanted to briefly discuss how we are thinking about financing in the current environment. Given the recent interest rate volatility and broader inflation, we remain focused on a financing strategy that preserves flexibility and supports long term value creation. Northwest Natural Gas, which represents the largest portion of our needs, benefits from a predictable capital program that generally requires only modest debt financing each year. That allows us to remain flexible and opportunistic as we access capital markets. Across the company, we have maintained very limited exposure to floating rate debt. Our target remains 10% or less. #3116. Google Search Isn’t Your Only Option. Try One of These Other Free Search Engines Now

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Online > Online Services

These free Google alternatives make it easy to break up with the tech giant.

On Tuesday, Nov. 3, Google announced that starting next year AI tools will be turned off by default in software used by K-12 students. Teachers and administrators will have to enable the features for students to use them in Google Search.

“Search and AI are deeply integrated,” Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, said, according to the New York Times. He also said if a school bans Google’s AI tools, students “will not have access to Search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

If you’re a parent or educator, you should know you don’t have to use Google Search to teach your children. There are plenty of other free search engines you can try now.

It’s also important to note that using these search engines in Google Chrome may prevent you from getting their full benefits. Here are five free alternatives to Google Search.

Brave also offers other features, like a VPN, a crypto wallet and its own AI assistant named Leo. And Brave said your AI usage is private and secure as well. You don’t even need to create or log into an account to use Leo.

This private, Berlin-based search engine is also a green option. Ecosia writes online it has planted over 250 million trees and produces more clean energy than it takes to power all its searches and AI queries. The company also writes online that all its profits go toward climate action.

This French-based search engine writes online it doesn’t retain your search data or sell your personal data, making it a good alternative to Google. In addition to search, Qwant also offers a feature called Qwant Junior, which it writes online is meant to help children between the ages of 6 and 12 years old safely explore the internet.

You should know that Qwant has integrated AI into its engine in what it calls Flash Answers. But you can deactivate it from your Settings menu without jumping through hoops. Historically, Qwant has used Bing’s search API, which lets companies access Bing’s search infrastructure. But according to CNBC, the company partnered with Berlin-based search engine Ecosia in 2024 to build a European search index in order to reduce dependence on US companies.

Startpage is a search engine that’s also a search aggregator. That means it partners with other companies like Google and Microsoft Bing to bring you search results.

For more on other search engines, here’s what to know about DuckDuckGo and Brave Search.

#3115. NASA unveils mysterious X-70 experimental aircraft using AI-generated image

NASA’s X-70 Fractal announcement comes as agency aims to grow X-plane fleet.

NASA has announced a new experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, that will supposedly feature reconfigurable flight-control technology and a modular design for swapping in different payloads. But much remains unknown about the aircraft’s design and development timeline, even as NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said the X-plane could take flight within two years.

The mystery surrounding NASA’s newest X-plane was exemplified by the agency’s press release, including an apparently AI-generated image of the X-70, showing a dark silhouette vaguely resembling a military fighter jet obscured by smoke. The news was announced by Isaacman during the UP.Summit held at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on November 4.

“The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” Isaacman said. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next.”

NASA’s press release described the X-70 as a crewed aircraft designed to cruise at Mach 0.75 while reaching a maximum altitude of up to 45,000 feet, and having an operational range beyond 1,726 miles (2,778 kilometers). The article did not mention a specific aircraft manufacturer that might be helping the agency develop the X-plane.

The X-70 would also have a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds (4,536 kilograms) and a design capable of accommodating up to 2,000 pounds (907 kilograms) of experimental payloads both internally and externally. Ars has reached out to NASA for more details.

Another X-plane is also expected to be announced at the UP.Summit on November 6, according to Aviation Week. That would coincide with a scheduled announcement from President Donald Trump at the event.

This comes after Isaacman previously appeared in front of another smoke-shrouded silhouette image with the tagline “Rebuilding our X-plane portfolio” during the All-In Summit in Los Angeles held from September 12–14, according to TWZ. That silhouette appeared strikingly similar to the SR-71 Blackbird that flew Cold War reconnaissance missions at supersonic speeds in the stratosphere.

Rumors have circulated about a possible revival of the SR-71 in one form or another, after former NASA employees told Aviation Week they received job offers to help restore an SR-71 to operational flight capability.

In September, the publication also reported on the removal of a NASA-owned SR-71 with the tail number 844 that had stood on display at NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center inside Edwards Air Force Base in California.

Meanwhile, NASA recently commemorated the first flight anniversary of its supersonic X-59 Quesst, a needle-nosed aircraft designed by Lockheed Martin to reduce sonic booms to sonic thumps. Ars has previously looked at how this X-plane program is intended to support the design of future supersonic airliners that may fly overland while minimizing disturbances for buildings and people below.

Since first taking to the skies on October 28, 2025, the X-59 has completed over 40 flight tests, including both low-speed flights and supersonic test runs reaching Mach 1.53, according to NASA. Such testing has taken place at NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center inside Edwards Air Force Base in California.

The X-59 also recently completed its first cross-country journey from California to Florida with stopovers in Texas and Alabama, accompanied by an F-15 and an F/A-18 from the agency’s research fleet that served as chase planes. It sat on the ground as a static display during the NASA Max Power airshow at Kennedy Space Center in Florida from November 7–8.

The supersonic aircraft will resume its test flight schedule once it returns to Armstrong Flight Research Center in California, a NASA spokesperson told Ars. Given the agency’s latest X-plane push, the X-59 may not be flying alone for many more years.
